# Ed’s Tokenized Securities Rails
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/index
description: Tokenized securities, explained with sources: a human-curated, LLM-maintained wiki on issuers, legal structures, custody, venues, settlement and regulation.
type: home
last_checked: 2026-10-30

# Tokenized securities, explained with sources.

A human-curated, LLM-maintained, source-linked knowledge base on **tokenized securities infrastructure**: issuers, legal structures, custody, chains, venues, settlement and regulation. Every fact links to a source; unverified fields say `unknown`.

- [Start with the overview](/overview)
- [Try a starter prompt](/starter-prompts/)
- [Browse the database](/database)

## What is this wiki?
A reference on how stocks and bonds move onto blockchains: who issues the tokens, what you legally own, where they trade, how they settle and which rules apply. It's reference information, updated weekly. What it isn't: a broker or investment advice.

[![How tokenized securities work in four steps: issue, approve buyers, trade and settle, pay holders. Opens the overview](/diagrams/overview-desktop.svg)](/overview)

*How it fits together, in one picture: [[overview|see the overview]].*

## Who is this for?
- **Investors:** what a stock token really gives you, who can buy, the risks. Start with the [[overview|overview]] and the [[concepts/glossary|glossary]].
- **Capital-markets people:** how issuance, trading, settlement and custody map to the rails you know. Start with [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]].
- **Crypto people:** the securities rules, issuers and venues behind tokenized stocks. Start with [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]].
- **Software engineers and architects:** a design reference for building these systems, especially trading, with your AI coding agents. Start with [[build/index|Build with this wiki]].
- **AI agents:** machine-readable via [llms.txt](/llms.txt) ([[concepts/glossary#llmstxt|what's that?]]) and the [[agents|guide for AI agents]], with sources on every fact and stable page anchors.

## Why tokenize securities?
- **Cash and asset swap in one step.** Both sides settle together or not at all ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp260826~3641116314.en.html)).
- **Markets don't need to close.** Trades could clear in seconds, 24/7 ([BlackRock](https://www.blackrock.com/corporate/investor-relations/2025-larry-fink-annual-chairmans-letter)).
- **Assets plug into other things,** such as collateral for futures and swaps ([CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9146-25)).
- **It's already real:** about \$368B of repo settles daily on Broadridge's platform ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2025/broadridge-distributed-ledger-repo-platform-november)), and about \$14.5B of tokenized Treasuries are held onchain ([rwa.xyz](https://app.rwa.xyz/treasuries)).

The full case, and the catches, are in [[overview#why-tokenize-securities|the overview]].

# Tokenized securities: how it fits together
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/overview
description: How tokenized securities fit together (issuance, trading, settlement, custody, regulation), why tokenize, and what is new compared with traditional rails.
type: overview
last_checked: 2026-10-30

<picture>
<source media="(max-width: 700px)" srcset="/diagrams/overview-mobile.svg">
<img src="/diagrams/overview-desktop.svg" alt="How tokenized securities work in four steps: issue, approve buyers, trade and settle, pay holders; plus native token versus wrapper" style="width:100%;height:auto">
</picture>

*Terms in this diagram: [[concepts/glossary#native-token|native token]], [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapper]], [[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]], [[concepts/glossary#atomic-settlement|atomic]], [[concepts/glossary#t1|T+1]], [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]]. [See the detailed version](#the-full-picture)*

## What is a tokenized security?
A tokenized security is an ordinary stock or bond whose ownership record lives on a shared digital ledger, so trading, settling and paying dividends can run automatically.

## Why tokenize securities?
Today, buying a stock or bond goes through a chain of brokers, [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodians]] and [[concepts/glossary#ccp|clearinghouses]]. Each one keeps its own records and has to reconcile them with the others, which is why settlement takes days and markets close at night. A token puts the asset and its ownership record on one shared ledger, so:

- **Cash and asset swap in one step.** Both sides settle together or not at all ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp260826~3641116314.en.html)).
- **Markets don't need to close.** Trades could clear in seconds, 24/7 ([BlackRock](https://www.blackrock.com/corporate/investor-relations/2025-larry-fink-annual-chairmans-letter)).
- **Assets plug into other things.** Tokenized Treasuries can already be posted as collateral for futures and swaps ([CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9146-25)).
- **More people get access.** You can own fractions, from anywhere.

It's already real for big institutions, though two common numbers measure different things. About \$368B of repo trades *settle every day* on Broadridge's blockchain platform: that is a daily flow, with the same cash and bonds lent and repaid over and over ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2025/broadridge-distributed-ledger-repo-platform-november)).

Tokenized Treasuries *held* on blockchains total about \$14.5B as of Oct 2026: that is a stock of assets, like an account balance ([rwa.xyz](https://app.rwa.xyz/treasuries)). Most tokenized assets so far are bonds and [[concepts/glossary#money-market-fund|money market funds]] ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).

Many stock tokens are wrappers: a third party holds the real share and gives you a token that tracks it, usually without a vote ([[overview#native-vs-wrapped|native vs wrapper]]).

## What's actually different from today's rails
- **One shared record instead of many copies.** Today the official list of who owns a share sits with a [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] or central depository, and every bank and broker in between keeps its own copy that has to be checked against the others. With tokens, everyone works from the same ledger, and the token balance can be the official record. The BIS says this joins "messaging, reconciliation and asset transfer into a single, seamless operation" ([BIS AER 2025, ch. III](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)). A transfer agent often stays involved for regulatory reasons ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).
- **Cash and asset swap at the same moment.** If the payment is also a token on the same ledger, one transaction can move the security one way and the cash the other: both happen or neither does. This is called [[concepts/glossary#atomic-settlement|atomic]] [[concepts/glossary#dvp|delivery versus payment]] (DvP) ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)). The digital cash can be central bank money, tokenized bank deposits or [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoins]] ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)), and which one is used changes the risk ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)). More: [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]].
- **The rules travel with the token.** Securities law still applies, so the token itself can refuse a transfer to a [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallet]] that has not passed identity checks, and the issuer can freeze or recover tokens. ERC-3643 is one standard that works this way ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)). See [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]], [[standards/erc-1400|ERC-1400]], [[standards/solana-token-2022|Token-2022]].
- **Always open, and reusable.** The ledger never closes, and the same token can be plugged into other uses such as collateral or lending ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). The flip side is that tightly linked systems can pass problems along; WEF flags the risk of "limitless composability" ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)).

## Native vs wrapped
There are two ways to put a share on a ledger, and which one you hold decides what you actually own.
- **Native: the token is the share.** The company, or its transfer agent, issues the security on the ledger, and your token balance is the official ownership record ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf); [SEC staff, 28 Jan 2026](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)). Examples: [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate Opening Bell]], [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] transfer-agent issuances.
- **Wrapper: a claim on a share.** The real share stays with a custodian or broker in the traditional system, and a third party issues a token that tracks it. SEC staff split wrappers into custodial ones (a claim on the held share) and [[concepts/glossary#synthetic-wrapper|synthetic]] ones (a separate contract, such as a note or swap) ([SEC staff](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)). Someone has to keep the number of tokens matched to the shares held, and you can only swap back through the issuer ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)).

> **Downsides of holding a wrapper.**
> - You own a claim on a firm that holds the share, not the share itself.
> - Usually no voting rights ([SEC staff](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).
> - You rely on that firm to keep the share safe and to [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeem]] it ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)). If it fails, you can lose money even if the company behind the share is fine: Robinhood warns its EU stock-token buyers they could lose up to their full investment if Robinhood becomes insolvent ([Robinhood EU](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/)).
> - The token can trade at a different price from the share.
> - The company behind the share may not have agreed: 22 companies had objected to tokens of their shares on OKXICE by 23 Oct 2026 ([[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv#issuer-objections|OKXICE objections]]).

The legal wrapper decides what the holder actually owns. More: [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy]], [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]] and [[comparisons/implementations-by-model|implementations by model]].

## The full picture
The same four steps in detail: who does what at each step, the traditional role each part replaces, and how native and wrapped tokens differ.

<picture>
<source media="(max-width: 700px)" srcset="/diagrams/overview-detailed-mobile.svg">
<img src="/diagrams/overview-detailed-desktop.svg" alt="Detailed diagram of how tokenized securities work. 1 Issue: the issuer and transfer agent create a security token on a shared 24/7 ledger. 2 Approve buyers: an identity allowlist means only KYC'd wallets can hold it. 3 Trade + settle: 3a Match on a trading venue (order book, RFQ or an onchain pool, also called an AMM or automated market maker); 3b Check the wallet allowlist and pre-funded legs; 3c Settle by atomic DvP, swapping the security token for a cash token in one transaction; 3d Record balances and update the register. 4 Pay holders: dividends, votes and redemptions go to investor wallets. A side panel contrasts native tokens (the token is the register) with wrapped tokens (a 1:1 claim on a share held by a custodian)." style="width:100%;height:auto">
</picture>

*Terms in this diagram: [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]], [[concepts/glossary#allowlist|allowlist]], [[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]], [[concepts/glossary#ats|ATS]], [[concepts/glossary#rfq|RFQ]], [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|onchain pool (AMM)]], [[concepts/glossary#smart-contract|smart contract]], [[concepts/glossary#prefunding|pre-funded]], [[concepts/glossary#netting|netting]], [[concepts/glossary#atomic-settlement|atomic]], [[concepts/glossary#dvp|DvP]], [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]], [[concepts/glossary#tokenized-deposit|tokenized deposit]], [[concepts/glossary#t1|T+1]], [[concepts/glossary#ccp|CCP]], [[concepts/glossary#csd|CSD]], [[concepts/glossary#composability|composable]], [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]], [[concepts/glossary#native-token|native]], [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]].*

## The four steps in the diagram
1. **Issue.** The issuer, or its transfer agent, creates tokens and keeps them in sync with the official register. For wrappers, a custodian holds the underlying shares.
2. **Approve buyers.** Investors are checked once ([[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]]) and their wallets are added to an [[concepts/glossary#allowlist|allowlist]], and every transfer checks the list. This replaces part of what opening an account does today. See [[topics/who-can-buy|Who can buy]].
3. **Trade + settle.** This is where tokenized rails differ most from today's, so it is broken into four parts below.
4. **Pay holders.** Dividends, splits, votes and redemptions run through the token contract or the issuer's agent. See [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|Corporate actions & dividends]] and [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]].

## Inside step 3: trade and settle
- **3a Match.** Orders still meet on a familiar venue, such as an exchange or [[concepts/glossary#ats|ATS]] order book or a broker's [[concepts/glossary#rfq|RFQ]], or in an [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|onchain pool]] or AMM, as in [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|permissioned pools]] and the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|onchain-venue (TSV) model]]. Matching can happen off-chain with only settlement on the ledger, or entirely on-chain. Several US models keep the traditional book and tokenize post-trade only: see the [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|post-trade / Reg NMS model]] and the [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTC tokenization pilot]].
- **3b Check (pre-trade).** The token contract checks that the receiving wallet is eligible ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)). Because on-ledger settlement is usually trade by trade (gross), both legs typically have to be in place up front. Projects that "eliminate principal counterparty risk" do so by requiring "high levels of liquidity, often through [[concepts/glossary#prefunding|prefunding]] on a platform" ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)), rather than the [[concepts/glossary#netting|netting]] and credit that today's CCPs and brokers provide.
- **3c Settle.** A [[concepts/glossary#smart-contract|smart contract]] swaps the security token for the cash token in one transaction, so both legs settle or neither does ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)). IOSCO describes a range of settlement models. At one end the ledger is only shared books and records, and [[concepts/glossary#settlement-finality|settlement finality]] "remain[s] with the [[concepts/glossary#csd|CSD]]". At the other is DLT-native settlement, with assets and settlement instruments on the same ledger or linked ones ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). Finality is still a legal question, not just a technical one: final settlement "is a legally defined moment" ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)).
- **3d Record (post-trade).** Wallet balances update at once. For [[concepts/glossary#native-token|native tokens]] that is the register update. For wrapped tokens, or where a transfer agent keeps the official register, the books must still be updated or reconciled against the ledger ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/); [IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). Regulatory reporting still applies.

**Trade-offs.**
- **Pre-funding.** It removes settlement exposure but costs liquidity. The FSB warns that higher prefunding needs at scale could weaken resilience to liquidity shocks ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)). IOSCO notes that CCP functions such as netting could in time be encoded in smart contracts ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).
- **Market hours.** An always-on ledger does not make 24/7 trading automatic. WEF calls always-on infrastructure "a design choice dependent on market demand, risk tolerance and technology" ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)).
- **Cash leg.** The choice of cash token matters. The CPMI-IOSCO principles favour central bank money where practical and available, as cited by [WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/).

## Mapping to familiar roles
| TradFi role | Tokenized equivalent |
|---|---|
| Registrar / transfer agent / CSD | Token contract (native) or custodian plus token (wrapped); transfer agent often remains ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)) |
| Account opening / KYC | Identity registry and allowlist ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)) |
| Exchange / ATS / broker | Same roles, or an onchain venue |
| CCP netting + T+1 settlement via CSD | Pre-funded, trade-by-trade atomic DvP on the ledger ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)) |
| Cash in bank or central bank accounts | Tokenized deposits, wholesale CBDC or stablecoins ([WEF](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/)) |
| Brokerage account | Custodial or self-held wallet ([[topics/custody|Custody]]) |

## Formal definitions
CPMI: "the process of generating and recording a digital representation of traditional assets on a programmable platform" ([CPMI 2024](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d225.htm)). IOSCO: the "creation, issuance, or representation of assets on a digital token ledger or a programmable platform" ([IOSCO 2025](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).

## Where it stands
Adoption is real but early. IOSCO finds it "incipient and incremental," led by fixed income and money market funds (see the [[comparisons/buidl-precedent|BUIDL precedent]]). A lack of cross-chain interoperability and of credible settlement assets limits scale, and many participants still use traditional trading and post-trade infrastructure ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)).

The FSB sees no material stability risk at today's small scale. It names liquidity and maturity mismatch, leverage, asset quality, interconnectedness and operational fragility as the vulnerabilities to watch ([FSB](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf)). The BIS argues for a "unified ledger" with tokenised central bank reserves, commercial bank money and government bonds at its centre ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm)).

Regulators broadly apply "same activities, same risks, same regulatory outcomes" ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf)). For the US and EU specifics, see [[topics/regulation|Regulation]] and [[concepts/international|International]].

## Text version of the diagram
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S1[1 Issue: company or agent creates tokens on a shared ledger] --> S2[2 Approve buyers: only KYC-checked wallets can hold]
  S2 --> S3[3 Trade + settle: 3a match, 3b check wallet, 3c token and cash swap at once, 3d record]
  S3 --> S4[4 Pay holders: dividends, votes, redemptions]
  N[Native: the token is the share] -.- S1
  W[Wrapper: a third party holds the share; the token is a claim on it] -.- S1
```

*Reference information only. Not investment advice.*

# Guide for AI agents
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/agents
description: How AI agents should read, query and cite this wiki on the live site.
last_checked: 2026-10-30

Ed’s Tokenized Securities Rails is a human-curated, LLM-maintained, source-linked knowledge base on tokenized securities infrastructure. This page is for AI agents reading the live site. Working from a clone of the repo? Read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/edyavno/edstokenizedsecuritiesrails/blob/main/AGENTS.md) instead.

## Fast ways in
- [`https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms.txt`](https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms.txt): one line per page with a short summary.
- [`https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms-full.txt`](https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms-full.txt): every page in one plain-text file.
- [[starter-prompts/index|Starter prompts]]: example questions this wiki can answer, plus [[starter-prompts/coding-agents|prompts for coding agents]].

## URL patterns
| URL | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/<page>` | Companies that issue tokenized securities or stock tokens |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/platforms-venues/<page>` | Exchanges, trading venues and exchange rule filings |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/infrastructure/<page>` | Settlement, oracle, DeFi and tokenization infrastructure |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/<page>` | Token standards (ERC-3643, ERC-1400, Token-2022, B20) |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/<page>` | Legal and market-structure concepts |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/<page>` | Cross-cutting explainers (custody, settlement, regulation, ...) |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/<page>` | Side-by-side comparisons of models and precedents |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/build/<page>` | For engineers: reference architecture and how to build with this wiki |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/changelog/<page>` | Dated change entries |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/overview` | How the pieces fit together, with a diagram |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/database` | One table of all issuers, venues and infrastructure |
| `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/whats-changed` | Weekly headlines with what each change means for holders |

Folder URLs (e.g. `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/`) list their pages. Entity pages open with an **At a glance** box (type, jurisdiction, chain, status, last updated) and end with **Sources**. `unknown` means not yet verified from a public source.

## Freshness
The site updates weekly, as of each Monday 00:00 ET; [[whats-changed|What changed]] lists changes by week. Check each page's *last updated* date and confirm time-sensitive facts against the linked source.

## How to cite
- Cite the page URL and its last-updated (`last_checked`) date, e.g. "Ed’s Tokenized Securities Rails, *Dinari dShares*, https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/dinari (last updated 2026-10-17)".
- Link to a heading for a specific point. Headings are stable anchors: lowercase, spaces become hyphens, e.g. `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/build/trading-reference-architecture#key-rules` or `https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/glossary#dvp`.
- For a specific fact, cite the original source linked on the page (regulator, filing, standard, issuer docs), not only the wiki.
- If the page says `unknown`, report it as unknown; do not fill it in from elsewhere.
- Changelog entries marked *unconfirmed, news report only* are single news reports; say so when you use them.

## Every page has
- A clear `title`, a one-line `description` and a `last_checked` date in its YAML frontmatter.
- Plain markdown with inline source links and a **Sources** section.

## Engineers and coding agents
See [[build/index|Build with this wiki]] and the [[build/trading-reference-architecture|reference architecture for trading]].

## Licence
Content is CC BY-NC 4.0: free to use and share with attribution, not for commercial use. Reference information only; not investment advice.

# Starter prompts
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/starter-prompts/index
description: Copy-paste questions an AI assistant can answer from this wiki, plus prompts for AI coding agents.
type: hub
last_checked: 2026-10-30

Copy a prompt into your AI assistant. Each one is answerable from this wiki alone.

**Building software?** See [[starter-prompts/coding-agents|Prompts for coding agents]].

## Start every session with
```text
Read https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms-full.txt (or clone the site repo). Cite page URLs and last-updated dates, and say "unknown" rather than guess.
```

## Structures and rights
```text
Which issuers offer native shares on the issuer's register, and which offer wrapped or derivative tokens? Cite the page for each.
```

```text
Compare bStocks, xStocks and Robinhood Stock Tokens by legal structure, jurisdiction and who can buy.
```

```text
What rights does a holder of a Dinari dShare have compared with a Superstate Opening Bell holder?
```

## Venues and settlement
```text
How does Nasdaq's approved tokenized securities rule keep tokenized and traditional shares on the same order book?
```

```text
What does the DTC no-action letter allow, and which venue rules reference the DTC pilot?
```

```text
Summarize the OKXICE TSV design under the Innovation Exemption: access, pairs and custody.
```

## Standards and infrastructure
```text
Compare ERC-3643, ERC-1400 and Solana Token-2022 on how they enforce transfer restrictions.
```

```text
How do Chainlink tokenized equity feeds handle stock splits and multipliers?
```

```text
How do Uniswap v4 permissioned pools enforce issuer allowlists?
```

## Regulation and markets
```text
Which entities are US-regulated versus offered only outside the US? Build a table with jurisdiction and status.
```

```text
What does the SEC staff statement on tokenized securities say about issuer-sponsored versus third-party tokens?
```

```text
How are dividends and corporate actions handled across issuers? Note any that are `unknown`.
```

## Tips
- Ask the agent to cite page URLs and `last_checked` dates, and to say `unknown` rather than guess.
- The site updates weekly; check the linked sources for anything time-sensitive.

# Prompts for coding agents
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/starter-prompts/coding-agents
description: Copy-paste prompts for AI coding agents building tokenized-securities systems, each telling the agent to cite pages of this wiki.
type: hub
last_checked: 2026-10-30

*In plain English: ready-made prompts for AI coding agents. Each tells the agent to read this wiki first and cite the pages it relies on. A design reference, not legal advice.*

## Start every session with
```text
Read https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/llms.txt and /build/ before answering. Cite wiki page URLs with headings and last-updated dates, cite the original source for any rule, and say "unknown" rather than guess.
```

## Design
**Permissioned onchain pool under the SEC exemption**
```text
Design a permissioned AMM pool for tokenized US stocks that meets the SEC Innovation Exemption venue conditions (credentialed participants, issuer notice and objection, public contracts, halt mirroring, tier caps). Use /concepts/innovation-exemption and /build/trading-reference-architecture. For each condition, name the component that enforces it and cite the SEC order.
```

**End-to-end trading system**
```text
Using /build/trading-reference-architecture, propose an architecture for [my use case]. Choose onchain vs hybrid matching, the cash leg, native vs wrapper and the chain, and justify each choice with cited pages.
```


## Implement
**ERC-3643 compliance module**
```text
Add an ERC-3643 compliance module that limits [rule, e.g. holders per country]. Follow /standards/erc-3643. Implement canTransfer, transferred, created and destroyed, and write property tests for key rule 1 (only allowlisted wallets receive the token) in /build/trading-reference-architecture#key-rules.
```

**Multiplier handling**
```text
Make my integration multiplier-safe for stock tokens. Use /topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends: store raw amounts, display raw x multiplier, and handle scheduled updates. Add a test that a split does not change any holder's economic position.
```

**Halt controller**
```text
Implement a halt controller that pauses a pool when the primary exchange halts a symbol. Use /build/trading-reference-architecture#key-rules (rule 3) and cite the SEC order's stoppage-of-trading condition.
```


## Review
**Settlement flow review**
```text
Review this settlement flow against /topics/settlement-and-matching and /build/trading-reference-architecture#key-rules. List every way a leg could settle without the other, and what prefunding it needs.
```

**Mint/redeem review**
```text
Review my mint and redeem service against /build/trading-reference-architecture (mint/redeem and reconciliation). Check that token supply matches the real shares held on every chain I deploy to.
```

**Key risk review**
```text
List every admin key in my design and what it can do, using /topics/custody and /standards/erc-3643. Flag any single key that can move investor tokens.
```


See also [[starter-prompts/index|Starter prompts]] for research questions and [[build/index|Build with this wiki]].

# Glossary
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/glossary
description: Plain-English definitions of the jargon used on this wiki, from allowlist to wrapper.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-10-28

*In plain English: short definitions of the terms this wiki uses, A to Z. Each one links to a source and to the pages that go deeper.*

New to all of this? Start with the [[overview|overview]], then come back here when a word trips you up. Reference information only, not investment advice.

Jump to: [A](#a) · [B](#b) · [C](#c) · [D](#d) · [E](#e) · [F](#f) · [H](#h) · [I](#i) · [K](#k) · [L](#l) · [M](#m) · [N](#n) · [O](#o) · [P](#p) · [R](#r) · [S](#s) · [T](#t) · [U](#u) · [W](#w)

## A

### Admin keys
Keys that control privileged token functions, such as pausing, freezing a wallet, forcing a transfer or upgrading the contract. Who holds them, and how they are protected, is a core custody and governance question. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643 (T-REX)]] · [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### Allowlist
A list of approved wallet addresses. A permissioned token only moves to wallets on the list, which is how identity checks are enforced onchain. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643 (T-REX)]] · [[topics/who-can-buy|Who can buy]]

### AMM (automated market maker)
An onchain pool, also called a liquidity pool: a smart contract that holds two assets and sets prices by a formula, so traders swap against the pool instead of being matched with a buyer or seller. ([BIS CPMI](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d225.htm))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap v4 permissioned pools]] · [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model]] · [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]]

### Atomic settlement
Both sides of a trade settle in one indivisible step: either everything moves or nothing does. Atomic DvP is the common case. ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### ATS
An alternative trading system: an SEC-regulated venue run by a broker-dealer that matches orders but is not a full stock exchange. ([Figure](https://investors.figure.com/news-releases/news-release-details/figure-announces-chain-public-equity-network-open-running))

*Related:* [[issuers/figure-open|Figure OPEN]]

### Authorized Participant
A large firm, usually a market maker, allowed to create (mint) and redeem tokens directly with the issuer. Ordinary holders buy and sell on the market instead. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]] · [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase Tokenized Stocks]]

## B

### B20
The token standard on Base that Coinbase's tokenized stocks use. ([Base](https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]]

### Bankruptcy-remote
Set up so that if the parent company fails, its creditors cannot reach the assets held for token holders. ([Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/tokenize))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

### Base
A layer 2 blockchain built on Ethereum and run by Coinbase. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]] · [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase Tokenized Stocks]]

### Broker-dealer
A firm registered with the SEC to buy and sell securities for customers (broker) or for itself (dealer). Most people buy stocks through one. ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

## C

### Canton
A permissioned blockchain network built for financial institutions, with privacy between parties. TSV LLC plans to run its tokenized stock venue on Canton ([TSV LLC](https://www.tokenizedstockvenue.com/notice.html)), and DTCC's Tokenization Service runs on it, with CIP-56 as the token standard ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)).

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]]

### CIP-56
The token standard DTCC's Tokenization Service uses on the Canton Network (it uses ERC-20 on its private Besu network). ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC Tokenization Service]]

### CCP
A central counterparty, or clearinghouse. It steps between buyer and seller so each side faces it instead of each other, and nets trades to reduce how much cash and stock must move. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Cede & Co.
DTC's nominee. For most US shares held through brokers, it is the holder on the company's register. ([Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]] · [[concepts/glossary#street-name|Street name]]

### Compliance hook
Code that runs on every token transfer or swap and can block it if a rule fails, such as an unverified receiver. Examples: the ERC-3643 compliance contract, Solana transfer hooks and Uniswap v4 permissioned-pool hooks. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643); [Uniswap](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4-hooks/permissioned-pools/architecture))

*Related:* [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]] · [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]]

### Composability
Tokens on the same chain can plug into other apps, for example being posted as loan collateral, without special integration work. ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### Corporate action
An event the issuer causes that changes what a shareholder holds or gets: dividends, splits, mergers, votes. Wrapped stock tokens often handle them with a multiplier. ([xStocks](https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers))

*Related:* [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### CSD
A central securities depository: the institution that holds securities centrally and records who owns them at the top level. In the US that is DTC. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]]

### CUSIP
The 9-character ID code for a US security, like a serial number for a stock or bond. DTC-tokenized securities keep the same CUSIP as the book-entry security. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf); [DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html))

*Related:* [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model]]

### Custodial wrapper
A token backed one-for-one by a real share held at a custodian. You own a claim on that share, not the share itself. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

### Custodian
A regulated firm that holds assets for someone else. For wrapped tokens, the custodian holds the real shares behind the tokens. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

## D

### Digital Securities Sandbox
A UK Bank of England and FCA sandbox, running until January 2029, where firms can issue, trade and settle securities, native or tokenised, on new technology. ([Bank of England](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/financial-stability/digital-securities-sandbox))

*Related:* [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]]

### Direct Registration System (DRS)
DTC's system for moving shares between its nominee [[concepts/glossary#cede-co|Cede & Co.]] and the holder's own name on the issuer's books, kept by the [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]]. DTC has proposed cutting its processing "from days to minutes". ([SEC notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20301/self-regulatory-organizations-the-depository-trust-company-notice-of-filing-of-proposed-rule-change))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]] · [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]]

### DLT
Distributed ledger technology: a shared database copied across many computers. Blockchains are one type. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### DLT Pilot Regime
An EU framework that lets approved market infrastructures trade and settle tokenized securities on DLT with some rules relaxed. ([ESMA](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-06/ESMA75-117376770-460_Report_on_the_functioning_and_review_of_the_DLTR_-_Art.14.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]] · [[concepts/international|International regimes]]

### DTC
The Depository Trust Company, the US central securities depository. It runs a tokenization pilot under an SEC no-action letter. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]]

### DTCC
The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation, parent of DTC. It provides clearing and settlement for most US stock trades. ([DTCC](https://communications.dtcc.com/rs/669-QIL-921/images/DTCC%20Tokenization%20Service%20At-a-Glance.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]]

### DWAC
Deposit/Withdrawal at Custodian: a DTC process for moving shares in and out of DTC through the transfer agent. Securitize asked DTC to modernize it alongside DRS. ([Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/glossary#direct-registration-system-drs|Direct Registration System (DRS)]]

### DvP
Delivery versus payment: the security is delivered only if the payment is made. Onchain, both legs can move in one transaction (atomic DvP). ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

## E

### Entitlement token
A token that is a [[concepts/glossary#security-entitlement|security entitlement]] to a share held by a broker or custodian, backed 1:1. Securitize's version is a convertible entitlement token (CET): when the company adopts issuer-sponsored tokenization, holders can convert it into a share recorded on the company's register. ([Securitize](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html))

*Related:* [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] · [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]]

### ERC-1400
A draft Ethereum standard suite for security tokens, with transfer checks, documents and forced transfers. ([Spec](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-1400|ERC-1400 / ERC-1410]]

### ERC-20
The basic Ethereum token standard. Most tokens, including many stock tokens, follow it or extend it. ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview))

*Related:* [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]]

### ERC-3643
An Ethereum standard for permissioned tokens: a transfer only goes through if both wallets pass identity and compliance checks. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643 (T-REX)]]

### ETF
An exchange-traded fund: a fund whose shares trade on an exchange like a stock. ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/backeds-xstocks-go-live-today-on-bybit-kraken-and-solana-defi-302494374.html))

*Related:* [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks (Backed)]]

### Ethereum
A public blockchain that runs smart contracts. Many token standards (ERC-20, ERC-3643) were written for it. ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643))

*Related:* [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]]

### Exemptive relief
Permission from the SEC to do something an existing rule would otherwise forbid, usually with conditions. ([WisdomTree](https://ir.wisdomtree.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/777/wisdomtree-to-launch-247-trading-and-instant-settlement))

*Related:* [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree tokenized funds]] · [[topics/regulation|Regulation]]

## F

### FINMA
Switzerland's financial market regulator. It licenses DLT trading facilities under the DLT Act in force since 1 August 2021. ([FINMA](https://www.finma.ch/en/authorisation/fintech/dlt-handelssystem/))

*Related:* [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]]

### FSRA (ADGM)
The Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Abu Dhabi Global Market, a financial free zone in the UAE. bStocks are admitted to its Official List. ([ADGM prospectus](https://www.adgm.com/globalassets/market-disclosure/content/prospectus/btech-holdings-prospectus----11-june---nvidia-bstocks_06_11_2026_16-44-54.pdf))

*Related:* [[issuers/bstocks|bStocks]] · [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]]

## H

### Halt
A pause in trading a stock, ordered by the primary exchange or a regulator. TSVs must stop trading a token while its stock is halted. ([SEC order](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] · [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### Hybrid matching
Trades are matched off chain (for example on an order book) and then settled on chain, instead of being priced and settled by an onchain pool in one step.

*Related:* [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

## I

### Identity registry
The ERC-3643 contract that records which wallets belong to verified investors; a transfer only succeeds if the receiver is verified. ([ERC-3643 docs](https://docs.erc3643.org/erc-3643/smart-contracts-library/onchain-identities/identity-registry))

*Related:* [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]]

### Innovation Exemption
A temporary, conditional SEC order from 17 Sep 2026 that lets approved onchain venues (TSVs) trade tokenized US stocks. ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model]]

### Issuer-sponsored token
A tokenized share that the issuing company itself sponsors, tied directly to its official shareholder register so holders keep ownership rights, votes and corporate-action entitlements. ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

## K

### KYC
Know your customer: identity checks a firm must run before letting you open an account or hold certain assets. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/who-can-buy|Who can buy]]

## L

### Layer 2
A blockchain that runs on top of another (usually Ethereum) to make transactions cheaper and faster. Base is one. Also written L2. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]]

### llms.txt
A plain-text index of a website written for AI models: one line per page with a short summary. This wiki publishes one at [/llms.txt](/llms.txt). ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/))

*Related:* [[build/index|Build with this wiki]]

## M

### MiCA
The EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation. It covers crypto-assets that are not financial instruments, so tokenized shares usually fall under MiFID II instead.

*Related:* [[concepts/international|International regimes]] · [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]]

### MiFID II
The EU's main law for investment firms and trading venues. Tokenized shares and derivatives such as Robinhood's EU stock tokens are covered by it. ([Robinhood EU FAQ](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/))

*Related:* [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens|Robinhood Stock Tokens]] · [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]]

### Mint
To create new tokens. For backed stock tokens, tokens are minted when the matching shares are bought and put in custody. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[standards/b20|Coinbase B20]]

### Money market fund
A fund that invests in very short-term, low-risk debt such as Treasury bills. Many of the largest tokenized products are money market funds. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree tokenized funds]] · [[comparisons/buidl-precedent|BUIDL (adjacent fund precedent)]]

### Multiplier
A number that converts one token into shares of the underlying stock. It changes after splits or reinvested dividends so token balances stay the same while each token is worth more or fewer shares. Also called rebasing. ([xStocks docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers))

*Related:* [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|Corporate actions & dividends]]

## N

### Native token
A token that is the security itself: the token balance is the official register of who owns it. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### Netting
Adding up all of a firm's trades and settling only the difference. It cuts how much cash and stock must move, but needs a central party and time. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### NMS stock
A stock listed on a US national exchange and covered by Reg NMS, the rules that tie US stock markets together. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model]]

### No-action letter
A letter from SEC staff saying they will not recommend enforcement if a firm does a specific thing under stated conditions. It is not a rule change. ([SEC DTC no-action letter](https://www.sec.gov/files/tm/no-action/dtc-nal-121125.pdf))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]] · [[topics/regulation|Regulation]]

## O

### Onchain / offchain
Onchain means recorded and executed on the blockchain itself; offchain means handled in an ordinary system, such as a firm's database or matching engine, and possibly settled onchain later. ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### Opt-out (issuer objection)
Under the Innovation Exemption, a company's right to stop a venue (TSV) from trading a third-party token of its stock. It has 30 calendar days from the venue's notice to object, directly to that venue. Each objection covers only that venue; there is no blanket opt-out. ([Nasdaq FAQ](https://www.nasdaq.com/docs/listings/faq-sec-innovation-exemption))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] · [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]]

### Oracle
A service that feeds outside data into a blockchain so smart contracts can use it. For tokenized stocks that means a reference price plus market status (open, closed or halted), so a venue can stop trading when the primary market stops. ([Chainlink](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/tokenized-equity-feeds))

*Related:* [[infrastructure/chainlink-equity-feeds|Chainlink tokenized equity feeds]] · [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

## P

### Permissioned network
A blockchain where only approved operators run nodes and only approved parties join, unlike a public chain. Examples: Canton, and the Besu-based network DTCC uses for its Tokenization Service. ([DTCC](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html))

*Related:* [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### Permissioned pool
An AMM pool that only allowlisted wallets can trade in; a hook checks eligibility on every swap. It is the model the SEC's Innovation Exemption covers for TSVs. ([Uniswap](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4-hooks/permissioned-pools/architecture))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] · [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### Prefunding
Putting the full cash and the full securities in place before a trade, because atomic settlement leaves no time to borrow or net. It costs liquidity. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

## R

### Reconciliation
Regularly checking that two records agree, for example that tokens in circulation match the real shares held, or that the share register matches the chain. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### Redeem
To hand tokens back to the issuer in exchange for the underlying asset or its cash value. Usually limited to eligible holders or Authorized Participants. ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks))

*Related:* [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

### Reg NMS
Regulation National Market System: SEC rules that link US stock exchanges, including best-price and order-protection rules. ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model]]

### Registrar
The firm or system that keeps the official list of who owns a security. In the US this is usually the transfer agent.

*Related:* [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]] · [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]]

### Repo
A repurchase agreement: a short-term loan where one side sells bonds and agrees to buy them back later at a slightly higher price. ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2025/broadridge-distributed-ledger-repo-platform-november))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

### RFQ
Request for quote: you ask one or more dealers for a price and trade at the quote you accept, instead of using a public order book. ([Robinhood](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Rule 15c3-3
The SEC customer protection rule. It requires broker-dealers to keep customers' securities in their possession or control and separate from the firm's own. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

### RWA
Real-world asset: a traditional asset such as a bond, fund or stock represented as a token. ([rwa.xyz](https://app.rwa.xyz/treasuries))

*Related:* [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

## S

### Security entitlement
The legal right, under UCC Article 8, of someone who holds a security through a broker or custodian rather than directly on the company's register. Securitize Stocks are security entitlements backed 1:1 by shares. ([Securitize](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html))

*Related:* [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

### Settlement finality
The point at which a transfer can no longer be reversed and ownership has legally changed. ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Slippage
The gap between the price you expect and the price you actually get, which grows when an order book is thin. Coinbase research flags it as higher for tokenized stocks than for the underlying shares, especially outside market hours. ([Coinbase Institutional](https://www.coinbase.com/institutional/research-insights/research/market-intelligence/major-trends-in-tokenization))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement and matching]] · [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase Tokenized Stocks]]

### Smart contract
A program stored on a blockchain that runs automatically when its conditions are met, for example a swap that only completes if both sides pay. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/token-primitives|Token primitives]]

### Solana
A public blockchain known for fast, low-cost transactions. Its Token-2022 program supports compliance features. ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions))

*Related:* [[standards/solana-token-2022|Solana Token-2022 extensions]]

### Soulbound token
A non-transferable token tied to one wallet, used as an access credential. OKXICE's venue notice uses soulbound tokens to control who can trade. ([OKXICE notice](https://www.okx.com/cdn/assets/files/2610/798CC1267CB56FB2.pdf))

*Related:* [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]]

### SPV
A special purpose vehicle: a company set up only to hold certain assets or issue certain securities, kept separate from its parent. ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory))

*Related:* [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]] · [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo Global Markets (Ondo Stocks)]]

### Stablecoin
A token designed to keep a steady value, usually one US dollar, backed by cash and short-term government debt. ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Street name
Holding shares through a broker, with DTC's nominee [[concepts/glossary#cede-co|Cede & Co.]] as the holder on the company's register instead of the investor. ([Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/glossary#direct-registration-system-drs|Direct Registration System (DRS)]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

### Synthetic wrapper
A token that is a separate security, such as a note or swap, that tracks a stock's price. It may not be backed one-for-one by real shares. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]]

## T

### T+1
Trade date plus one business day: the current US settlement cycle for most stock trades. ([FSB 2024](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P221024-2.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Token-2022
Solana's newer token program, with add-ons such as transfer hooks and frozen-by-default accounts that support permissioned tokens. ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions))

*Related:* [[standards/solana-token-2022|Solana Token-2022 extensions]]

### Tokenized deposit
A bank deposit represented as a token. It is a claim on a regulated bank, unlike a stablecoin. ([WEF 2025](https://www.weforum.org/publications/asset-tokenization-in-financial-markets-the-next-generation-of-value-exchange/))

*Related:* [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]

### Transfer agent
The firm a company appoints to keep its official register of shareholders and record transfers. ([IOSCO](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD809.pdf))

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]] · [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate Opening Bell]] · [[infrastructure/vertalo|Vertalo]]

### Transfer hook
Code that runs automatically on every token transfer, for example to check the receiving wallet is allowed. ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook))

*Related:* [[standards/solana-token-2022|Solana Token-2022 extensions]]

### TSV
Tokenized Securities Venue: an onchain venue approved under the SEC's Innovation Exemption to trade tokenized US stocks. ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model]] · [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]]

## U

### Unified ledger
A BIS proposal for one programmable platform holding tokenised central bank reserves, commercial bank money and government bonds, so payments and securities settle together. ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

### Uniswap v4 hooks
Add-on code that a Uniswap v4 pool calls before or after swaps; used to build permissioned pools that check an allowlist. ([Uniswap](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4-hooks/permissioned-pools/architecture))

*Related:* [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] · [[build/trading-reference-architecture|Reference architecture for trading]]

## W

### Wallet
Software or hardware that holds the keys controlling tokens. A custodial wallet is run by a firm; a self-custody wallet is run by you.

*Related:* [[topics/custody|Custody]]

### Wholesale CBDC
Central bank money in token form, used only between banks and financial firms for settlement, not by the public. ([BIS](https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm))

*Related:* [[concepts/international|International regimes]]

### Wrapper
A token that represents a share held by someone else, rather than being the share itself. See custodial wrapper and synthetic wrapper. ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities))

*Related:* [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities]] · [[overview|Tokenized securities: how it fits together]]

# What changed
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/whats-changed
description: Weekly headlines on tokenized securities, with a note on what each change means for holders.
last_checked: 2026-10-30

The week's changes in tokenized securities, newest first. Each headline links to its changelog entry and sources; where the sources support it, a line says what the change means for people who hold the tokens.

Grouped by week (weeks start Monday), newest first. Every publish shows every change recorded so far, including the current week.

## Get it by email
A free weekly email with these headlines. [[subscribe|Subscribe]].

## This week (in progress)
- **[New front page and a starter-prompts hub](/changelog/2026-10-30-front-page-and-starter-prompts)**
  - *What this means for holders:* No change to any facts. The site is easier to start with: a short front page, one place for copy-paste prompts, and the overview now covers only how it fits together.
- **[SIFMA's comment letter on the Innovation Exemption](/changelog/2026-10-29-sifma-comment-letter)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Wall Street's main trade group wants companies to opt in before third-party tokens of their stock can trade. See [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]].
- **[Ondo Stocks live on Robinhood Chain](/changelog/2026-10-29-ondo-stocks-robinhood-chain)**
  - *What this means for holders:* On Robinhood Chain you can now swap some Robinhood Stock Tokens for the matching Ondo token, which Ondo redeems 24/7, including weekends. See [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo]].
- **[OKXICE objections reach 38; how issuer opt-outs work; Better Markets letter](/changelog/2026-10-29-okxice-38-objectors-opt-out)**
  - *What this means for holders:* More big companies, including JPMorgan, Coca-Cola and Walmart, have blocked third-party tokens of their stock on OKXICE. An objection only covers one venue. See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]].
- **[DTCC Tokenization Service goes live](/changelog/2026-10-28-dtcc-tokenization-service-live)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Large brokers can now turn shares held at DTC into tokens and back, same CUSIP and same rights. See [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]].
- **[QRT, Vertalo and zerohash join the Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition](/changelog/2026-10-26-coalition-new-members)**
  - *What this means for holders:* More firms, including a transfer agent, now back issuer-sponsored tokens. See [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]].
- Database: 5 headline field updates across issuer, venue and token records.

## Week of 19 Oct 2026
- **[OKXICE objectors now 22; DTCC launch scope 34; Figure ticker FGRS; B20 spec](/changelog/2026-10-25-sources-pass)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Issuer objections can keep a stock off OKXICE, and 22 issuers had objected by 23 Oct 2026. See [[concepts/innovation-exemption#issuer-objection|Issuer objection]].
- **[Securitize asks DTC to link direct registration to its tokenization service](/changelog/2026-10-25-securitize-drs-comment)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Issuer-sponsored tokens depend on fast moves out of DTC. See [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]].
- **[DTCC launch scope; OKXICE issuer objections; Robinhood Chain volume](/changelog/2026-10-23-dtcc-okxice)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Companies can object to a third-party token of their stock on OKXICE; objections can keep a stock off the venue. See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]].
- **[Kraken says xStocks lineup exceeds 1,000 (unconfirmed, news report only)](/changelog/2026-10-22-kraken-xstocks-1000)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Unconfirmed, news report only: a news site reports more than 1,000 xStocks on Kraken; Kraken has not confirmed this on its own pages. Check Kraken's xStocks list before relying on it.
- **[OCC final rule implementing the GENIUS Act](/changelog/2026-10-21-occ-genius-rule)**
- **[TSV LLC revises its TSV notice](/changelog/2026-10-19-tsv-llc-revised-notice)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Nothing trades yet; when TSV LLC opens, pools will settle against USDC or SBC on Canton. See [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]].
- Database: 45 headline field updates across issuer, venue and token records.

- **[Vault seeded with 15 entities](/changelog/2026-10-17-vault)**
- **[Perpetuals.com files a TSV notice](/changelog/2026-10-14-perpetuals-notice)**
- Database: 68 headline field updates across issuer, venue and token records.

## Week of 5 Oct 2026
- **[EU Council agrees key elements of the market integration package](/changelog/2026-10-09-eu-council-dlt-pilot)**
- **[Securitize launches tokenized US stocks on Solana](/changelog/2026-10-08-securitize-stocks)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Securitize's tokens are security entitlements, a direct claim on custodied shares. See [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]].
- **[Ondo tokenized stocks reach EEA investors via Assetera](/changelog/2026-10-07-assetera-ondo)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Eligible investors in 30 EEA countries can buy Ondo tokens through a MiFID II platform. See [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo Global Markets]].
- **[DTC proposes faster direct registration (DRS)](/changelog/2026-10-05-dtc-drs-modernization)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Moving shares into your own name could take minutes instead of days. See [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]].

## Week of 28 Sep 2026
- **[OKXICE files its TSV notice](/changelog/2026-10-04-okxice-notice)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Companies can object to OKXICE tokens of their stock. See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]].

## Week of 21 Sep 2026
- **[Coinbase tokenized stocks accepted as Aave collateral](/changelog/2026-09-25-aave-coinbase-stocks)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Eligible non-US holders of seven Coinbase stock tokens can borrow USDC against them on Aave V4 on Base. See [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase tokenized stocks]].
- **[Bullish and Equiniti form the Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition](/changelog/2026-09-24-issuer-sponsored-token-coalition)**
  - *What this means for holders:* A new industry group backs tokens tied to the company's own shareholder register, so holders keep voting and dividend rights. See [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]].
- **[CFTC staff FAQs allow tokenized permitted investments](/changelog/2026-09-24-cftc-tokenized-collateral-faq)**
- **[First TSV notice filed with the SEC (TSV LLC)](/changelog/2026-09-23-tsv-llc-notice)**

## Week of 14 Sep 2026
- **[SEC issues the Innovation Exemption for tokenized NMS stock](/changelog/2026-09-17-sec-innovation-exemption)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Tokenized US stocks can trade on exempt Tokenized Securities Venues, subject to caps and issuer objection. See [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]].
- **[UK tokenisation feedback; Robinhood plans redemption and voting](/changelog/2026-09-14-fca-robinhood)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Robinhood Stock Tokens still give price exposure only; in-kind redemption and voting are announced, not available. See [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens|Robinhood Stock Tokens]].

## Week of 7 Sep 2026
- **[Nasdaq agrees to invest in Kraken's parent for tokenized equities](/changelog/2026-09-10-nasdaq-payward)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Nasdaq Equity Tokens are planned, not live; Nasdaq and Payward expect them in Q2 2027. See [[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq tokenized securities]].

## Week of 17 Aug 2026
- **[Kraken opens US stocks and xStocks to EEA customers](/changelog/2026-08-18-kraken-eea-stocks)**
  - *What this means for holders:* Eligible EEA customers can hold ordinary US shares and xStocks in one Kraken account. See [[platforms-venues/kraken|Kraken]].

## Week of 10 Aug 2026
- **[Crypto.com launches tokenized stock derivatives in the EEA](/changelog/2026-08-12-crypto-com-tokenized-stocks)**
  - *What this means for holders:* These are derivatives: you get price exposure only, with no shares and no votes. See [[issuers/crypto-com-tokenized-stocks|Crypto.com Tokenized Stocks]].
- **[Bullish trades its own tokenized shares on a GFSC-regulated exchange](/changelog/2026-08-12-bullish-tokenized-equity)**
  - *What this means for holders:* BLSH tokens are real registered shares, but only Bullish's own stock trades this way so far. See [[platforms-venues/bullish|Bullish Exchange]].

## Week of 15 Jun 2026
- **[SEC notice: 24X Exchange tokenized trading rule (SR-24X-2026-20)](/changelog/2026-06-16-sec)**

## Week of 16 Mar 2026
- **[SEC approves Nasdaq tokenized securities rule](/changelog/2026-03-18-sec)**
  - *What this means for holders:* A tokenized share traded on Nasdaq keeps the same CUSIP, symbol and shareholder rights as the regular share. See [[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq]].

## Week of 23 Feb 2026
- **[WisdomTree announces 24x7 trading for WTGXX](/changelog/2026-02-24-wisdomtree)**
  - *What this means for holders:* WTGXX holders can trade fund shares around the clock with instant settlement, under SEC exemptive relief. See [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree]].

## Week of 1 Dec 2025
- **[Kraken agrees to acquire Backed Finance AG](/changelog/2025-12-02-kraken)**

## Week of 30 Jun 2025
- **[xStocks live on Bybit, Kraken, Solana DeFi](/changelog/2025-06-30-xstocks)**
  - *What this means for holders:* xStocks are 1:1-backed certificates issued by Backed Assets (Jersey), not shares: no voting rights, and not offered in the US, Canada, UK or Australia. See [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]].

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

# Rules by jurisdiction
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/rules-by-jurisdiction
description: In plain English: Where tokenized securities stand under the rules in each place this wiki tracks, in one table.
type: topic
last_checked: 2026-10-25

*In plain English: Where tokenized securities stand under the rules in each place this wiki tracks, in one table.*

Each row gives the status and the main rule or regulator guidance, linked to the regulator's own document. **Not yet collected** means this wiki has no source for that place yet; it does not mean there are no rules. 0 of 12 jurisdictions are not yet collected.

| Jurisdiction | Status | Main rule or guidance | Last checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| United States (federal) | Rules in force | [SEC Innovation Exemption for tokenized NMS stock (Rel. 34-106402)](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf) | 2026-10-25 |
| United States (states) | Rules in force | [State securities acts apply to tokenized securities; Wyoming UCC treatment of digital securities](https://www.wyoleg.gov/2019/Enroll/SF0125.pdf) | 2026-10-25 |
| European Union | Pilot or sandbox | [DLT Pilot Regime (ESMA recommends making it permanent and wider)](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-06/ESMA75-117376770-460_Report_on_the_functioning_and_review_of_the_DLTR_-_Art.14.pdf) | 2026-10-25 |
| United Kingdom | Pilot or sandbox | [Digital Securities Sandbox (Bank of England and FCA)](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/financial-stability/digital-securities-sandbox) | 2026-10-25 |
| Switzerland | Rules in force | [DLT Act (FinMIA Chapter 4a, DLT trading facilities)](https://www.finma.ch/en/authorisation/fintech/dlt-handelssystem/) | 2026-10-25 |
| Singapore | Regulator guidance | [MAS Guide on the Tokenisation of Capital Markets Products](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/guidelines/guide-on-tokenisation-of-cmps) | 2026-10-25 |
| Hong Kong | Regulator guidance | [SFC circular on tokenised securities-related activities (23EC52)](https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/doc?refNo=23EC52) | 2026-10-25 |
| UAE (ADGM) | Regulator guidance | [FSRA Guidance on Regulation of Digital Securities Activities (digital securities are Securities under FSMR)](https://assets.adgm.com/download/assets/guidance-on-regulation-of-digital-securities-activities-in-adgm.pdf/f57b23cc3a0a11ef857b6e984d6ae48f) | 2026-10-25 |
| UAE (Dubai and federal) | Rules in force | [Federal CMA Virtual Assets Framework (April 2026); Dubai VARA rulebooks outside DIFC](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bzp2c5q-capital-market-authority-issues-virtual-assets) | 2026-10-25 |
| Jersey | Regulator guidance | [JFSC guidance on tokenisation of real world assets (COBO consent; issuer domicile for xStocks and Robinhood Stock Tokens)](https://www.jerseyfsc.org/industry/guidance-and-policy/tokenisation-of-real-world-assets-rwas/) | 2026-10-25 |
| British Virgin Islands | Rules in force | [VASP Act 2022 and SIBA (issuer domicile for Ondo Global Markets)](https://www.bvifsc.vg/news/industry-updates/virtual-assets-service-providers-act-2022) | 2026-10-25 |
| Gibraltar | Rules in force | [GFSC-regulated DLT exchange (Bullish) approved for tokenized securities trading](https://investors.bullish.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bullish-launches-tokenized-equity-trading) | 2026-10-25 |

**Status key.** *Rules in force*: a rule, order or licence regime that applies now. *Pilot or sandbox*: a time-limited or capped regime. *Regulator guidance*: guidance on how existing securities law applies to tokens. *Proposed*: filed or proposed, not yet approved.

For the detail behind each row, see [[topics/regulation|Regulation]], [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] and [[concepts/international|International]].

*Reference information only, not investment advice or legal advice.*
