# Reference architecture for trading tokenized securities
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/build/trading-reference-architecture
description: End-to-end reference architecture for trading tokenized stocks on tokenized rails: onboarding and allowlisting, onchain or hybrid matching, compliance hooks, atomic DvP, register sync, and oracle and halt controls.
type: build
last_checked: 2026-10-25

*In plain English: an overview of how a tokenized-stock trading system fits together, from letting an investor in, through the trade, to updating the official record. Deeper pages on each part will be added as the roadmap ships.*

## End-to-end components
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Access["1 · Access"]
      KYC["KYC /<br/>onboarding"] --> REG["Identity registry<br/>/ allowlist"]
      WAL["Wallets<br/>and keys"]
    end
    subgraph Trading["2 · Trading"]
      VEN["Onchain venue:<br/>permissioned pool"]
      HYB["Hybrid:<br/>offchain match"]
      ORA["Oracle and<br/>halt controller"]
    end
    subgraph Asset["3 · Asset"]
      TOK["Token contract<br/>+ compliance hook"]
      CASH["Cash token: stablecoin<br/>or tokenized deposit"]
    end
    subgraph Records["4 · Records"]
      MR["Mint / redeem<br/>+ reconciliation"]
      TA["Transfer agent / register<br/>or custodian"]
      CA["Corporate actions:<br/>multiplier"]
    end
    WAL --> VEN
    WAL --> HYB
    ORA --> VEN
    VEN --> TOK
    HYB --> TOK
    TOK --> REG
    VEN --> CASH
    TOK --> TA
    MR --> TOK
    MR --> TA
    CA --> TOK
    CA --> ORA
    classDef access fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
    classDef trading fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f
    classDef asset fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    classDef records fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#4c1d95
    class KYC,REG,WAL access
    class VEN,HYB,ORA trading
    class TOK,CASH asset
    class MR,TA,CA records
    style Access fill:#eff6ff,stroke:#2563eb
    style Trading fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#d97706
    style Asset fill:#f0fdf4,stroke:#16a34a
    style Records fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#7c3aed
```
Terms: [[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]] · [[concepts/glossary#allowlist|allowlist]] · [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallets]] · [[concepts/glossary#admin-keys|keys]] · [[concepts/glossary#permissioned-pool|permissioned pool]] · [[concepts/glossary#hybrid-matching|hybrid matching]] · [[concepts/glossary#onchain--offchain|offchain]] · [[concepts/glossary#oracle|oracle]] · [[concepts/glossary#halt|halt]] · [[concepts/glossary#compliance-hook|compliance hook]] · [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]] · [[concepts/glossary#tokenized-deposit|tokenized deposit]] · [[concepts/glossary#mint|mint]] · [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeem]] · [[concepts/glossary#reconciliation|reconciliation]] · [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] · [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] · [[concepts/glossary#corporate-action|corporate actions]] · [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]]

Colors: **blue** = access, **amber** = trading, **green** = asset and cash, **purple** = records.

## One trade, end to end
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant I as Investor<br/>wallet
    participant K as KYC /<br/>registry
    participant O as Oracle +<br/>halt control
    participant V as Venue: pool<br/>or matcher
    participant T as Stock token<br/>+ compliance
    participant C as Cash<br/>token
    participant R as Transfer<br/>agent
    rect rgb(219, 234, 254)
    Note over I,K: Onboard
    I->>K: onboard
    K-->>I: wallet allowlisted
    end
    rect rgb(254, 243, 199)
    Note over I,O: Order and pre-trade checks
    I->>V: order or swap
    V->>O: symbol open?<br/>price fresh?
    O-->>V: open / halted
    end
    alt halted or stale
        V-->>I: reject
    else open
        rect rgb(220, 252, 231)
        Note over V,C: Settle: atomic DvP, both legs or neither
        V->>T: canTransfer<br/>(seller, buyer)?
        T->>K: both verified?
        K-->>T: yes
        V->>T: deliver stock token
        V->>C: deliver cash
        end
        rect rgb(237, 233, 254)
        Note over T,R: Record
        T-->>R: transfer event
        Note over R: update<br/>register,<br/>reconcile
        end
    end
```
Terms: [[concepts/glossary#dvp|DvP]] · [[concepts/glossary#atomic-settlement|atomic settlement]] · [[concepts/glossary#oracle|oracle]] · [[concepts/glossary#halt|halted]] · [[concepts/glossary#compliance-hook|compliance]] · [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] · [[concepts/glossary#reconciliation|reconcile]]

Phases: **blue** = onboard, **amber** = order and checks, **green** = atomic settlement, **purple** = record. Same colors as the component map above.

## Components
| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| Token contract + [[concepts/glossary#compliance-hook|compliance hook]] | Only eligible wallets can hold or receive |
| [[concepts/glossary#mint|Mint]] / [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeem]] + [[concepts/glossary#reconciliation|reconciliation]] | Supply matches real shares |
| Venue ([[concepts/glossary#permissioned-pool|permissioned pool]] or [[concepts/glossary#hybrid-matching|hybrid]]) | Matches and settles trades |
| [[concepts/glossary#oracle|Oracle]] + [[concepts/glossary#halt|halt]] control | Fresh prices; stop when the stock is halted |
| [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|Transfer agent]] / register | The official record stays in sync with the chain |

## Key rules
1. Only allowlisted wallets ever receive the stock token ([ERC-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)).
2. Both legs of a trade settle or neither does ([[concepts/glossary#atomic-settlement|atomic settlement]]).
3. No trading while the primary exchange has the stock halted ([SEC order](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf)).

> [!note] vs traditional trading infrastructure
> Traditional trading uses broker order routing, exchange order books or RFQ, CCP netting and T+1 settlement at DTC, with eligibility enforced by brokers and the transfer agent. Tokenized rails move eligibility into the token, settle atomically and run 24/7. See [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]] and [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|Post-trade (Reg NMS) model]].

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf>
- <https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4-hooks/permissioned-pools/architecture>
- <https://www.tokenizedstockvenue.com/notice.html>
- <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643>
- <https://www.bis.org/publ/arpdf/ar2025e3.htm>
- <https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html>
- <https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/tokenized-equity-feeds>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf>

# Innovation Exemption and the onchain-venue (TSV) model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/innovation-exemption
description: In plain English: The SEC now lets a few approved onchain venues trade tokens of US stocks, for a limited time and under conditions.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-10-29

*In plain English: The SEC now lets a few approved onchain venues trade tokens of US stocks, for a limited time and under conditions. This page explains how that works and who objects.*

On 17 Sep 2026 the SEC issued an order (Rel. 34-106402, File 4-927) granting temporary, conditional section 36(a)(1) relief ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf); [press release](https://business.cch.com/srd/SECgov_SECIssuesInnovationExemptiontoFacilitatetheTradingofTokenizedNMSStockandRequestforComment091726.pdf)):
- **Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs)** operating permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|AMM]] liquidity pools are exempt from the definition of "exchange".
- **Covered Firm** liquidity providers are exempt from the definition of "dealer".
- **Conditions** include U.S. person and OFAC compliance, a 30-day public notice, issuer notice and objection for third-party tokens, same rights as the underlying, public auditable [[concepts/glossary#smart-contract|smart contracts]] on a permissionless ledger, and synchronized halts ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf)).
- **Caps**: Tier 1 cannot exceed 75 symbols and 0.25 percent of prior-month average daily share volume; Tier 2 cannot exceed 250 symbols and 2.5 percent ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf); [Skadden](https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/09/sec-innovation-exemption-establishes)).
- Synthetics are excluded; the order expires five years after publication ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf)).

Chairman Atkins framed it as a bridge to durable rulemaking ([statement](https://business.cch.com/srd/SECgov_StatementontheInnovationExemption_ABridgeTowardDurableRulemaking091726.pdf)). Law-firm analyses: [Skadden](https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/09/sec-innovation-exemption-establishes), [Davis Polk](https://www.davispolk.com/insights/client-update/sec-s-innovation-exemption-opens-path-tokenized-stock-trading), [WilmerHale](https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/client-alerts/20261005-the-innovation-exemption-arrives-sec-clears-a-conditional-path-for-onchain-trading-of-tokenized-nms-stocks).

## TSV notices
The SEC lists three TSV notices: TSV LLC (23 Sep 2026), OKXICE TSV (4 Oct 2026) and Kephas Corporation d/b/a Perpetuals.com (14 Oct 2026) ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/about/divisions-offices/division-trading-markets/innovation-exemption)). None had started trading by 25 Oct 2026 per their notices and the SEC page. TSV LLC revised its notice on 19 Oct (v1.1) and 23 Oct 2026 (v1.2): it will run on Canton with USDC and SBC as paired assets at commencement, and the issuer's transfer agent handles participant verification and minting ([TSV LLC](https://www.tokenizedstockvenue.com/notice.html)).

## Issuer objection
For third-party tokens, the issuer gets notice and can object during the 30-day window ([SEC order](https://business.cch.com/srd/34-106402091726.pdf)). Explainer applied to the first notice: [Dida Labs](https://didalabs.com/tokenized-stock-objection/) (analysis). First test: by 21 Oct 2026, 16 issuers, including Goldman Sachs, Microsoft, Alphabet and McDonald's, had objected to OKXICE listings ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tokenized-stocks-us-companies-object.html), news). By OKXICE's 28 Oct notice the count was 38, including JPMorgan, Coca-Cola, Walmart and Eli Lilly ([OKXICE notice, 28 Oct](https://www.okx.com/cdn/assets/okfe/web3-activities/okxicetsv/notices/OKXICE_Tokenized_Securities_Venue_Public_Notice_26.10.28.pdf)).

How the opt-out works for issuers, per Nasdaq's FAQ ([Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/docs/listings/faq-sec-innovation-exemption), last updated 29 Sep 2026): the TSV must send notice to the address of the issuer's principal executive offices on its Exchange Act reports; the issuer has 30 calendar days from receipt to object; the objection goes directly to that venue, and Nasdaq can't file it for them. Notices and [[concepts/glossary#opt-out-issuer-objection|opt-outs]] are per TSV, with no blanket opt-out. Nasdaq says it intends to opt Nasdaq, Inc. out of TSVs, and warns that TSVs don't have to show best prices or report trades until 10 minutes after they happen.

The contrast CNBC draws: offshore volume is mostly perps and [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]] tokens that never needed issuer permission, while the US path gives issuers a say ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tokenized-stocks-us-companies-object.html)). See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv]].

## Industry response
A week after the order, Bullish and Equiniti formed the [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]], citing the requirement that venues verify a token gives holders the same rights as the traditional share ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

## Comment file (4-927)
Better Markets, an investor advocacy nonprofit, filed a 13-page letter on 22 Oct 2026. It calls TSVs and the dealer exemption the largest rewrite of secondary equity trading rules since [[concepts/glossary#reg-nms|Reg NMS]], argues such changes need APA notice-and-comment rulemaking (with cost-benefit analysis) rather than an order, and urges the SEC to withdraw or rescind the order. It also asks that third-party tokens require the issuer's affirmative consent instead of an opt-out ([Better Markets](https://bettermarkets.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Better-Markets-Comment-Letter-SEC-Innovation-Exemption.pdf), raw/155).

SIFMA, the broker-dealer and asset manager trade group, filed an initial letter on 19 Oct 2026 (signed by CEO Kenneth Bentsen). Unlike Better Markets it does not ask for withdrawal; it asks the SEC to amend the order and answer operational questions. Its asks: trading of third-party tokens only with the issuer's affirmative consent (opt-in); failing that, an official SEC- or FINRA-run portal listing TSVs, their notices and issuer elections, a 90-day objection period from confirmed receipt, and a single universal issuer opt-out; and the right to object at any time, even after trading starts. It also asks about surveillance (CAT, ISG), volume limits across venues, beneficial ownership and corporate actions, and says it would support the SEC giving venues more time before they begin operating ([SIFMA](https://www.sifma.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SIFMA-Innovation-Exemption-Initial-Letter-10-19-2026.pdf), raw/158).

## Stablecoin legs
TSV pools pair against payment [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoins]]; the GENIUS Act (S.1582, P.L. 119-27) defines permitted payment stablecoins and 1:1 reserves ([GENIUS Act](https://www.congress.gov/119/bills/s1582/BILLS-119s1582enr.htm)). The Act takes effect on 18 Jan 2027; the OCC's final rule for issuers under its jurisdiction takes effect the same day ([OCC](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-50.html); [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21706/implementing-the-guiding-and-establishing-national-innovation-for-us-stablecoins-act-for-the), FR Doc. 2026-21706).

First notice: [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]]. Primitive: [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap permissioned pools]].

# International regimes
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/international
description: In plain English: How rules for tokenized securities differ outside the US, region by region.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: How rules for tokenized securities differ outside the US, region by region.*

**EU [[concepts/glossary#dlt|DLT]] Pilot Regime**: ESMA's 2025 review found low uptake, with only [[concepts/glossary#csd|CSD]] Prague, 21X and 360X authorised; barriers include thresholds, interoperability, central-bank money and legal uncertainty. ESMA recommends making the regime permanent and wider ([ESMA report](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-06/ESMA75-117376770-460_Report_on_the_functioning_and_review_of_the_DLTR_-_Art.14.pdf); [ESMA press](https://www.esma.europa.eu/press-news/esma-news/esma-suggests-amendments-dlt-pilot-regime-make-it-permanent)).
**Offshore issuer domiciles** in this wiki: Jersey (xStocks, Robinhood), BVI (Ondo), ADGM (bStocks, Coinbase). See [[topics/regulation|regulation]].
Not yet collected: MiCA/[[concepts/glossary#mifid-ii|MiFID II]] detail, UK [[concepts/glossary#digital-securities-sandbox|Digital Securities Sandbox]], Swiss DLT Act, Singapore, Hong Kong.

For one table of rules by country, see [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]].

- <https://www.esma.europa.eu/press-news/esma-news/esma-suggests-amendments-dlt-pilot-regime-make-it-permanent>

# Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition
description: Industry working group formed by Bullish and Equiniti in Sep 2026 to set standards for issuer-sponsored tokenized securities.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-10-28

*In plain English: A group of exchanges, brokers and market firms working on rules and plumbing so companies can put their own shares onchain, with holders keeping the same rights as normal shareholders.*

Bullish and Equiniti formed the Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition on 24 Sep 2026, a week after the SEC's [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)). It backs the [[concepts/glossary#issuer-sponsored-token|issuer-sponsored token]] model, where the token is tied to the company's official shareholder register kept by its [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

## Members
- **Founding (24 Sep 2026):** Bullish and Equiniti, with Alpaca, Apex Fintech Solutions and DriveWealth ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).
- **Joined 26 Oct 2026:** Qube Research & Technologies (QRT), [[infrastructure/vertalo|Vertalo]] and [[infrastructure/zerohash|zerohash]] ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition-gains-momentum-as-qrt-vertalo-and-zerohash-join)).

Membership is open, non-exclusive and non-binding: joining does not commit a firm to issue, list, provide liquidity or support any product ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

Founding members Alpaca, Apex (as Apex Clearing Corporation) and DriveWealth are also among the 20 DTC participants signed for the DTCC Tokenization Service at its 28 Oct 2026 launch ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]]; [DTCC](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live)).

## Focus areas
1. Keep issuer and shareholder rights, including [[concepts/glossary#corporate-action|corporate-action]] entitlements.
2. Interoperability across traditional clearing and settlement, blockchains, [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]]-token models and emerging [[concepts/glossary#entitlement-token|entitlement-token]] frameworks. Example: Securitize's convertible entitlement token, which converts to a registered share once the issuer sponsors tokenization ([[issuers/securitize|Securitize]]).
3. Infrastructure for issuance, transfer, settlement, custody and trading.
4. An open ecosystem of issuers, brokers, exchanges, transfer agents, custodians and market makers.

([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities))

## Getting shares onto the register
Issuer-sponsored tokens need shares moved out of [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]]'s nominee [[concepts/glossary#cede-co|Cede & Co.]] and into the holder's own name, via the [[concepts/glossary#direct-registration-system-drs|Direct Registration System (DRS)]]. DTC has proposed cutting DRS processing "from days to minutes", expected 13 Nov 2026 and no later than January 2027 ([SEC notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20301/self-regulatory-organizations-the-depository-trust-company-notice-of-filing-of-proposed-rule-change)). Securitize's comment letter asks DTC to link DRS to its own tokenization service and publish processing times ([[issuers/securitize|Securitize]]; [Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf)).

## What's next
Members were due to meet issuers at the New York Stock Exchange on 27 Oct 2026 ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition-gains-momentum-as-qrt-vertalo-and-zerohash-join)). More members and initiatives were promised "in the coming weeks" ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

Related: [[platforms-venues/bullish|Bullish]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]] · [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|Corporate actions & dividends]]

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live>
- <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20301/self-regulatory-organizations-the-depository-trust-company-notice-of-filing-of-proposed-rule-change>
- <https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf>
- <https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities>
- <https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition-gains-momentum-as-qrt-vertalo-and-zerohash-join>

# Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/legal-taxonomy
description: In plain English: The SEC sorts tokenized stocks into a few legal types. This page explains each one, because the type decides what you actually own.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: The SEC sorts tokenized stocks into a few legal types. This page explains each one, because the type decides what you actually own.*

The SEC staff statement of 28 Jan 2026 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)) is the vocabulary used throughout this wiki:
- **Issuer-sponsored tokenization**: the issuer (or its agent) integrates [[concepts/glossary#dlt|DLT]] into its securityholder records; the onchain record is, or feeds, the master securityholder file. Examples: [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate Opening Bell]], [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] transfer-agent issuances.
- **Third-party tokenization**, split into:
  - **Custodial / security entitlement**: a third party holds the security and the token evidences an entitlement (e.g. UCC Article 8). Examples: Securitize Stocks, Coinbase [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]], [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] Tokenized Entitlements ([[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|post-trade model]]).
  - **Synthetic / linked**: the token is a separate security (e.g. a note) or security-based swap referencing the stock. Examples: Ondo Stocks (notes), Robinhood Stock Tokens (debt securities), bStocks (certificates).
- Format does not change legal obligations ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities); analysis: [Sidley](https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2026/01/sec-staff-unveils-a-playbook-for-tokenized-securities), [Jones Day](https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2026/02/sec-staff-provides-its-views-on-taxonomies-associated-with-tokenized-securities)).

## Broker-dealer custody
[[concepts/glossary#rule-15c3-3|Rule 15c3-3]] possession-and-control applies to crypto asset securities. The 2020 special-purpose [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]] statement is not mandatory ([SEC TM FAQ](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/trading-markets-frequently-asked-questions/frequently-asked-questions-relating-crypto-asset-activities-distributed-ledger-technology)). The 17 Dec 2025 TM statement describes how a broker-dealer establishes physical possession. It covers:
- the ability to transfer the asset
- private-key protections
- network risk assessment
- contingency plans

Sources: [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers); [Sidley](https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2025/12/sec-issues-further-crypto-asset-security-guidance-addresses-broker-dealer-physical-possession).

See also [[comparisons/implementations-by-model|implementations compared by model]].

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities>
- <https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2026/01/sec-staff-unveils-a-playbook-for-tokenized-securities>
- <https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2026/02/sec-staff-provides-its-views-on-taxonomies-associated-with-tokenized-securities>
- <https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/trading-markets-frequently-asked-questions/frequently-asked-questions-relating-crypto-asset-activities-distributed-ledger-technology>
- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers>
- <https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2025/12/sec-issues-further-crypto-asset-security-guidance-addresses-broker-dealer-physical-possession>

# Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model
description: In plain English: In this model a tokenized share is the same share as the normal one.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: In this model a tokenized share is the same share as the normal one. It trades on the same exchanges and only the record-keeping behind it changes.*

In this model the security does not change: tokenized and traditional shares share one order book, priority, CUSIP, symbol and rights, and settle through [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]]'s tokenization pilot ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)). Components:
- **DTC Tokenized Entitlements** under the 11 Dec 2025 [[concepts/glossary#no-action-letter|no-action letter]] ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]]).
- **Exchange rules**: [[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq]] (approved 18 Mar 2026), [[platforms-venues/nyse-ice-tokenized-platform|NYSE]].
Contrast with the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|onchain-venue model]] ([[concepts/glossary#tsv|TSVs]]).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/tm/no-action/dtc-nal-121125.pdf>
- <https://www.nyse.com/publicdocs/nyse/markets/nyse/rule-filings/sec-approvals/2026/%28SR-NYSE-2026-17%29_34-105260.pdf>

# Token primitives
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/token-primitives
description: In plain English: The basic technical building blocks that tokenized stocks are made of, and which projects use which.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: The basic technical building blocks that tokenized stocks are made of, and which projects use which.*

The building blocks used by tokenized-stock implementations:
- **Identity-gated transfers**: [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]] (identity registry + compliance), [[standards/erc-1400|ERC-1400]] (transfer validation, partitions), [[standards/solana-token-2022|Token-2022 transfer hooks]].
- **Plain ERC-20** with offchain eligibility: Robinhood Stock Tokens are standard ERC-20s ([Robinhood](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/)); Ondo uses ERC-20 on Ethereum/BNB Chain ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)).
- **[[concepts/glossary#multiplier|Multipliers]] for corporate actions**: build transactions in raw amounts, display raw x multiplier (xStocks, [docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers)); [[concepts/glossary#solana|Solana]] scaled UI amount; see [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|corporate actions]].
- **Permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|AMMs]]**: [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap v4 permissioned pools]].
- **[[concepts/glossary#oracle|Oracles]]** for a 24/5 underlying traded 24/7: [[infrastructure/chainlink-equity-feeds|Chainlink]].

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview>
- <https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers>

# Corporate actions & dividends
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends
description: In plain English: How dividends, stock splits and votes reach you depends on how the token is built. This page compares the approaches.
last_checked: 2026-10-27

*In plain English: How dividends, stock splits and votes reach you depends on how the token is built. This page compares the approaches.*

How a dividend or split reaches a token holder depends on the model (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Multiplier (rebasing) model
[[concepts/glossary#wrapper|Wrapped]] tokens usually reinvest dividends and raise a multiplier rather than pay cash.
- **xStocks**: dividends are reinvested net of withholding; splits and reverse splits scale the multiplier ([xStocks docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/dividends-and-stock-splits)). Kraken computes the change as the net dividend (after 30% US withholding) divided by the prior close, and updates it around 8 p.m. EST the day before the ex-date ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)). Holders get no voting rights.
- **Coinbase on Base ([[standards/b20|B20]])**: cash dividends are converted to shares and reflected in the multiplier (e.g. 1.02 means one token [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeems]] for 1.02 shares). Scheduled updates give advance onchain notice via ERC-8056 ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- Robinhood also uses multipliers that reflect reinvested dividends ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary).

## Issuer-sponsored and fund tokens
The token is the share, so corporate actions follow the register (Superstate). Exodus's tokens carry no economic rights of their own; those attach to the Class A share ([Exodus offering circular](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm)). WisdomTree's WTGXX accrues income daily and pays monthly in cash or [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]], or reinvests it ([WisdomTree FAQ](https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/)).

[[infrastructure/vertalo|Vertalo]], a [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] in the [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]], says [[concepts/glossary#issuer-sponsored-token|issuer-sponsored tokens]] work because the shareholder records and the token agree, and that agreement drives corporate actions ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition-gains-momentum-as-qrt-vertalo-and-zerohash-join)).

## DTC
At launch, [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pays Treasury distributions in fiat to participants' traditional accounts. Equity and [[concepts/glossary#etf|ETF]] corporate actions on tokens are on the 2027+ roadmap ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)).

## What this means for holders
- Wrapped tokens often reflect dividends and splits through a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] instead of cash; native shares and DTC-based tokens follow the normal share's corporate actions.
- Voting rights usually stay with the [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] or issuer for wrapped tokens; check each issuer page.
- Where a field says `unknown`, the sources so far do not say how that issuer handles it.

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/>
- <https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks>
- <https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/dividends-and-stock-splits>
- <https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq>
- <https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html>

# Custody
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/custody
description: In plain English: Who holds the real share, and who controls the token, differs by model. This page shows who keeps what.
last_checked: 2026-10-28

*In plain English: Who holds the real share, and who controls the token, differs by model. This page shows who keeps what.*

Who holds the real share, and who holds the keys, differs by model (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Backed (third-party) models
Backed models hold the underlying shares with a [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] or broker-dealer (Ondo: US broker-dealers; Dinari: registered US broker-dealer; Coinbase: bankruptcy-remote structure) ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary; [Fensory](https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms), secondary). SEC staff note that holders of third-party tokens may face risks, such as the third party's bankruptcy, that holders of the underlying share would not ([SEC staff statement, 28 Jan 2026](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).

## Issuer-sponsored models
These replace custody with a transfer-agent register: the token is the ownership record (see [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]], [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate]]).

## DTC tokenized entitlements
Tokens are backed 1:1 by securities held at [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]], and DTC keeps the official books and records ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC Tokenization Service]]; [DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)). The service went live on 28 Oct 2026, delivering tokens to participants' wallets of choice ([DTCC](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live)).

## Broker-dealer custody of tokens
SEC staff will not object to a broker-dealer treating itself as having "physical possession" of a crypto asset security under Rule 15c3-3(b)(1) if conditions are met, chiefly control of the private keys and safeguards against their theft or loss ([SEC staff statement, 17 Dec 2025](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers)). This is a staff statement, not a rule.

## Vendors
[[infrastructure/zerohash|Zerohash]] markets a tokenization engine to brokerages ([Zerohash](https://zerohash.com/industries/brokerages)).

## What this means for holders
- With a [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapper]], your protection depends on the issuer's [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] and whether the structure is [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]].
- Platform custody and token custody are separate questions: a venue can list a token without holding it (e.g. [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE]]).

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live>
- <https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/>
- <https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms>
- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers>
- <https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities>
- <https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html>
- <https://zerohash.com/industries/brokerages>

# Legal structures
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/legal-structures
description: In plain English: Tokenized stocks come in a few legal forms. Some are the real share; others are a claim or a note that tracks it.
last_checked: 2026-10-28

*In plain English: Tokenized stocks come in a few legal forms. Some are the real share; others are a claim or a note that tracks it.*

Tokenized stocks fall into distinct legal models ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/)):
- **Debt security / certificate** backed by shares (Robinhood, bStocks, xStocks).
- **Beneficial claim** on custodied shares (Coinbase [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]]; Securitize Stocks as [[concepts/glossary#security-entitlement|security entitlements]], convertible to registered shares).
- **Issuer-sponsored shares** recorded by a [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] (Securitize, Superstate Opening Bell).
- **Blockchain-native equity** (Figure FGRS).
- **Same security, tokenized form** inside the US market structure (Nasdaq / [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pilot, [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)).
Rights differ: backing does not automatically confer shareholder rights.

In the [[concepts/glossary#issuer-sponsored-token|issuer-sponsored]] model the token is tied to the company's official shareholder register, so voting, dividend and corporate-action rights carry over; wrapped and synthetic tokens only track the share. Most US shares sit in [[concepts/glossary#street-name|street name]], registered to DTC's nominee [[concepts/glossary#cede-co|Cede & Co.]]; moving them into the holder's own name runs through the [[concepts/glossary#direct-registration-system-drs|Direct Registration System (DRS)]], which DTC has proposed to speed up "from days to minutes" ([SEC notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20301/self-regulatory-organizations-the-depository-trust-company-notice-of-filing-of-proposed-rule-change)). Since Sep 2026 the [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]] has pushed this model ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

========================================================================
# Regulation
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/regulation
description: In plain English: The main US and international rule changes for tokenized securities, in date order.
last_checked: 2026-10-29

*In plain English: The main US and international rule changes for tokenized securities, in date order.*

Key US milestones: [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] [[concepts/glossary#no-action-letter|no-action letter]] (11 Dec 2025) and SEC approval of Nasdaq's tokenized trading rule (18 Mar 2026) ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)); WisdomTree's [[concepts/glossary#exemptive-relief|exemptive relief]] for 24/7 fund-share trading (Feb 2026, [WisdomTree](https://ir.wisdomtree.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/777/wisdomtree-to-launch-247-trading-and-instant-settlement)). Non-US issuers sit in Jersey, BVI and ADGM ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/)).

Recent changes (Sep to Oct 2026): the SEC's [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] for tokenized NMS stock (17 Sep 2026, [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-90-sec-issues-innovation-exemption-facilitate-trading-tokenized-nms-stock-request-comment)), which Better Markets' 22 Oct comment letter urges the SEC to withdraw in favor of notice-and-comment rulemaking ([Better Markets](https://bettermarkets.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Better-Markets-Comment-Letter-SEC-Innovation-Exemption.pdf)), while SIFMA's 19 Oct letter asks for amendments such as issuer opt-in consent and a 90-day objection period ([SIFMA](https://www.sifma.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SIFMA-Innovation-Exemption-Initial-Letter-10-19-2026.pdf)); CFTC staff FAQs on tokenized permitted investments (24 Sep 2026, [CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9303-26)); the OCC's final GENIUS Act rule, effective 18 Jan 2027 (21 Oct 2026, [OCC](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-50.html)); the FCA and Bank of England feedback statement FS26/1 (14 Sep 2026, [FCA](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/feedback-statements/fs26-1-tokenisation-wholesale-markets)); and EU Council agreement on key elements of the market integration package, which would widen the DLT Pilot Regime (9 Oct 2026, [Council](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/10/09/savings-and-investments-union-council-agrees-key-elements-of-crucial-measures-to-deepen-eu-capital-markets/)).

Country-by-country status: [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]].

# Settlement & matching
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/settlement-and-matching
description: In plain English: How tokenized stock trades get matched and settled, and how that differs from today's next-day settlement.
last_checked: 2026-10-28

*In plain English: How tokenized stock trades get matched and settled, and how that differs from today's next-day settlement.*

Tokenized stocks trade and settle in several ways (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Venue models
- **Centralized exchanges** list tokens: Kraken trades most xStocks 24/5, with 10 trading 24/7 on Kraken Pro; withdrawn tokens can trade 24/7 on DEXs ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)).
- **Onchain DEXs**: [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]] tokens trade permissionlessly in DeFi pools.
- **Tokenized Securities Venues** run permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|AMM]] pools under the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]]. Conditions include symbol and volume caps, a 30-day issuer objection window, and trading halts in step with the primary market ([SEC order 34-106402](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf)). See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]] and [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap permissioned pools]].
- **[[concepts/glossary#ats|ATS]]**: Figure's blockchain stock settles on Provenance in YLDS ([Figure 424(b)(4)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828026008786/figure-blockchain424b4.htm)); see [[issuers/figure-open|Figure OPEN]].
- **National exchanges** trade tokenized and traditional shares on one order book with equal priority, settled through [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] ([[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq]]; [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)).

## Post-trade
DTC's Tokenization Service went live on 28 Oct 2026 with 20 signed participants ([DTCC](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live)). It converts book-entry positions into tokens and back, 2 a.m.-6 p.m. ET on business days, targeting 15 minutes or less. Tokens then move peer-to-peer 24/7 between registered [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallets]] ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)). On-chain netting and digital cash are on the 2027+ roadmap.

## Liquidity and price risk
Coinbase Institutional's research team noted that tokenized-stock order books remain thin, with [[concepts/glossary#slippage|slippage]] and volatility significantly higher than in the underlying equity, especially post-market or under stress. It also flagged [[concepts/glossary#oracle|oracle]] errors or lags as a risk to token/collateral equivalence ([Coinbase Institutional](https://www.coinbase.com/institutional/research-insights/research/market-intelligence/major-trends-in-tokenization), 10 Jan 2026).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live>
- <https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/backeds-xstocks-go-live-today-on-bybit-kraken-and-solana-defi-302494374.html>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf>
- <https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html>
- <https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq>
- <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828026008786/figure-blockchain424b4.htm>

# Who can buy
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/who-can-buy
description: In plain English: Whether you can buy a given stock token depends on where you live and how the token is structured.
last_checked: 2026-10-25

*In plain English: Whether you can buy a given stock token depends on where you live and how the token is structured.*

Who can hold a tokenized stock depends on the structure (see [[overview|the overview]] and [[topics/legal-structures|legal structures]]).

## Offshore wrapped tokens
Most offshore products exclude US persons (xStocks, Ondo, Coinbase, Robinhood) ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary; [Fensory](https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms), secondary). [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]] are offered to eligible non-US clients in 110+ countries and are not available in the US, Canada, the UK or Australia ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)).

## US routes
- [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|Broker-dealer]] model: [[issuers/dinari|Dinari]] documents a US broker-dealer route.
- Issuer-sponsored shares can admit eligible US investors, usually behind KYC and a transfer-agent whitelist. Exodus token holders can only trade with holders who passed the [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]]'s AML/KYC and were whitelisted ([Exodus offering circular](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm)). WisdomTree's WTGXX allows transfers only between verified, whitelisted [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallets]] ([WisdomTree FAQ](https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/)).
- Tokenized Securities Venues under the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] are permissioned: access is limited to approved participants ([SEC order 34-106402](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf)).

## What this means for holders
- Most offshore tokens (xStocks, Ondo, Robinhood, Coinbase, bStocks) exclude US persons; check the issuer page for the exact country list.
- US routes run through registered firms: Dinari as [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]], Superstate as [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] for native shares, or exchange-listed tokenized shares via the [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pilot.
- Where you can buy is a property of the issuer and the platform together: see [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]].

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/>
- <https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms>
- <https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf>
- <https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/>
- <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm>

# Coinbase B20
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/b20
description: In plain English: B20 is the token format Coinbase uses for its tokenized stocks on Base.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-10-25

*In plain English: B20 is the token format Coinbase uses for its tokenized stocks on Base.*

B20 is the Base-native token standard that Coinbase's tokenized stocks use ([Base](https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks); [Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). It is designed to work for any asset; stocks are one use case.

## Design
- A superset of [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]], built as Rust precompiles and shipped in Base's Beryl upgrade ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)). Standard ERC-20 methods and events work.
- Two variants: **Asset** (6-18 decimals, with a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]]) and **[[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|Stablecoin]]** (6 decimals) ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).
- Built-in controls: transfer policies, freeze-and-reissue, roles, memos, supply caps and permit ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).
- Audited by Base and Spearbit, per the docs ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).

## Tokenized stocks on B20
- **Multiplier**: one token does not always equal one share. Cash dividends are converted to shares and the multiplier rises (e.g. 1.02) ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). Scheduled changes use ERC-8056 `updateUIMultiplier`; the instant `updateMultiplier` is deprecated and kept as a failsafe.
- **Identification**: integrators should identify tokens by contract address, not ticker, and watch the `B20Created` event. A public, keyless API returns addresses, supply, multipliers, ISINs and Chainlink reference values ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- **Access**: secondary transfers are permissionless; [[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]] applies to Authorized Participants who [[concepts/glossary#mint|mint]] and [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeem]] ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).

See [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase tokenized stocks]], [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|corporate actions]] and [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]] for a permissioned alternative.

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks>
- <https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20>
- <https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks>

========================================================================
# ERC-1400 / ERC-1410
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/erc-1400
description: In plain English: ERC-1400 is an older, draft set of Ethereum rules for security tokens that can block or force transfers.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: ERC-1400 is an older, draft set of Ethereum rules for security tokens that can block or force transfers.*

ERC-1400 (draft, 2018) is an umbrella suite: ERC-1594 (transfer validation, off-chain data), ERC-1643 (documents), ERC-1644 (controller/forced transfers) and ERC-1410 (partitions) ([spec](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md)). ERC-1410 defines balanceOfByPartition, transferByPartition and operator transfers, i.e. "partially fungible" balances useful for lockups and share classes ([ERC-1410](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1410.md)).

ConsenSys UniversalToken is a reference implementation with certificate-based validation ([GitHub](https://github.com/ConsenSys/ERC1400)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md>
- <https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1410.md>
- <https://github.com/ConsenSys/ERC1400>

========================================================================
# ERC-3643 (T-REX)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/erc-3643
description: In plain English: ERC-3643 is an Ethereum token standard that only lets approved, identity-checked wallets hold or receive the token.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: ERC-3643 is an Ethereum token standard that only lets approved, identity-checked wallets hold or receive the token.*

ERC-3643 is a final EIP. It extends the basic [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]] token with permissions: transfers can be conditional, paused or frozen, forced, or recovered.

A transfer only goes through if two checks pass ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)):
- the **Identity Registry** confirms both parties hold valid ONCHAINID claims, and
- the modular **Compliance** contract approves it.

Compliance modules cover limits such as country, holder count and balances ([ERC-3643 docs](https://docs.erc3643.org/erc-3643/smart-contracts-library/permissioned-tokens)). Reference implementation: [GitHub](https://github.com/ERC-3643/ERC-3643).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643>
- <https://docs.erc3643.org/erc-3643/smart-contracts-library/permissioned-tokens>
- <https://github.com/ERC-3643/ERC-3643>

# Solana Token-2022 extensions
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/solana-token-2022
description: In plain English: Token-2022 is Solana's token program with optional add-ons that tokenized stocks use for compliance and splits.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: Token-2022 is Solana's token program with optional add-ons that tokenized stocks use for compliance and splits.*

Token-2022 adds extensions including transfer hook, permanent delegate, default account state, scaled UI amount and metadata ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions)).
- **Transfer hook**: a custom program runs on every transfer; ExtraAccountMetaList resolves extra accounts. This is Solana's equivalent of identity-gated compliance checks ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook)).
- **Scaled UI amount**: a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] changes the displayed balance without changing raw balances; used for splits and reinvested dividends ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/scaled-ui-amount)).
Used by Ondo Stocks on Solana ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions>
- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook>
- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/scaled-ui-amount>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview>

# BUIDL (adjacent fund precedent)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/buidl-precedent
description: In plain English: BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, BUIDL, is an early example that later stock-token projects copied.
type: comparison
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, BUIDL, is an early example that later stock-token projects copied.*

BlackRock's BUIDL fund (launched 20 Mar 2024) used Securitize as [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]], tokenization platform and placement agent ([Nasdaq PR](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/blackrock-launches-its-first-tokenized-fund-buidl-on-the-ethereum-network-2024-03-20)). Adjacent to equities: a fund, not a stock. See also [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree]] (funds).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

# Implementations compared by model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/implementations-by-model
description: In plain English: A side-by-side table of tokenized stock projects, grouped by legal model.
type: comparison
last_checked: 2026-10-17

*In plain English: A side-by-side table of tokenized stock projects, grouped by legal model.*

Classification follows the [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|SEC staff taxonomy]]. Details and sources are on each linked page.

| Implementation | Model | Key mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell\|Superstate Opening Bell]] | Issuer-sponsored | SEC-registered transfer agent; onchain cap table |
| [[issuers/securitize\|Securitize (issuer shares)]] | Issuer-sponsored | Transfer agent book entry |
| [[issuers/securitize\|Securitize Stocks]] | Custodial entitlement | UCC Art. 8 via broker-dealer; Solana PropAMM |
| [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks\|Coinbase B20]] | Custodial claim | Beneficial claim; Alpaca custody |
| [[issuers/dinari\|Dinari dShares]] | Broker-dealer mirror record | Tokens mirror off-chain brokerage books |
| [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot\|DTC Tokenized Entitlements]] | Custodial entitlement (post-trade) | DTC participants; NAL |
| [[issuers/ondo-global-markets\|Ondo Stocks]] | Synthetic / note | BVI SPV notes; economic exposure |
| [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens\|Robinhood Stock Tokens]] | Synthetic / debt security | Jersey issuer; no rights in underlying |
| [[issuers/bstocks\|bStocks]] | Synthetic / certificate | ADGM certificates over shares |
| [[issuers/xstocks-backed\|xStocks]] | Backed tracker | Jersey issuer; multiplier |
| [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv\|OKXICE TSV]] | Venue (TSV) | Permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker\|AMM]] under Innovation Exemption |
| [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model\|Nasdaq / NYSE]] | Venue (exchange) | Same book, DTC settlement |

# Coinbase Tokenized Stocks
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks
description: In plain English: Coinbase's stock tokens on Base are each backed by a real share held in custody.
type: issuer
jurisdiction: Abu Dhabi Global Market (FSRA-authorized, per Coinbase via Zerion)
chain: Base
status: live
last_updated: 2026-10-17
last_checked: 2026-10-17

> [!info] At a glance
> **Type:** issuer  
> **Jurisdiction:** Abu Dhabi Global Market (FSRA-authorized, per Coinbase via Zerion)  
> **Chain:** Base  
> **Status:** live  
> **Last updated:** 2026-10-17  

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| name | Coinbase Tokenized Stocks |
| jurisdiction | Abu Dhabi Global Market (FSRA-authorized, per Coinbase via Zerion) |
| product_name | B20 stock tokens |
| structure | Beneficial claim on backing shares |
| chains | Base |
| who_can_buy | Eligible jurisdictions outside the US; offered under Regulation S |
| num_assets | 58 prospectuses listed on coinbase.com/tokenize (2026-10-17) |

*In plain English: Coinbase's stock tokens on Base are each backed by a real share held in custody.*

Each [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]] token on Base is a beneficial claim on a real share in [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]] custody ([Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/tokenize); [Base](https://www.base.org/stocks)). Coinbase holds an [[concepts/glossary#fsra-adgm|FSRA]] permission in ADGM ([ADGM](https://www.adgm.com/media/announcements/coinbase-establishes-its-tokenization-hub-in-abu-dhabi-with-financial-services-permission-from-the-financial-services-regulatory-authority)).

A public read-only API publishes records, [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multipliers]] and prospectuses ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/overview)).

[[concepts/glossary#authorized-participant|Authorized participants]] (institutional market makers) buy the shares, which go to Alpaca, a regulated broker and [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] ([Base](https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks); [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/08/24/coinbase-debuts-tokenized-stocks-on-base-network-joining-race-to-bring-equities-on-blockchain), news). Token format: [[standards/b20|B20]].

Since 25 Sep 2026, seven Coinbase tokenized stocks (AAPLc, AMZNc, GOOGLc, METAc, MSFTc, NVDAc, TSLAc) can be posted as collateral to borrow USDC on Aave V4 on Base ([Aave](https://www.aave.com/blog/coinbase-tokenized-stocks)).

John D'Agostino, head of strategy at Coinbase Institutional, said the initial offering covers about seven stocks and is planned to grow to 2,000 (a stated plan, not a launched figure) ([TheStreet via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/tokenized-stocks-turn-share-collateral-165759306.html), news, 27 Oct 2026).

## Coinbase research view (Jan 2026)
Coinbase Institutional's research team wrote that tokenized public equities were still under \$1B, versus about \$28B for tokenized Treasuries and private credit ([Coinbase Institutional, Major Trends in Tokenization](https://www.coinbase.com/institutional/research-insights/research/market-intelligence/major-trends-in-tokenization), 10 Jan 2026). It flagged three risks:
- **Market depth:** order books for tokenized stocks remain thin; [[concepts/glossary#slippage|slippage]] and volatility can be significantly higher than in the underlying stock, especially post-market or under stress.
- **[[concepts/glossary#oracle|Oracle]] risk:** off-chain prices must be brought onchain; errors, lags or manipulation can break the equivalence between token and underlying collateral.
- **Regulatory fragmentation:** jurisdictions differ on who can own what and how secondary transfers work.

The note says that if freely transferable designs are permitted, tokenized stocks could serve as collateral in lending markets; otherwise, with thin books, extended hours don't yet offset lower depth and higher friction ([Coinbase Institutional](https://www.coinbase.com/institutional/research-insights/research/market-intelligence/major-trends-in-tokenization)).

## What this means for holders
- A B20 stock token is a beneficial claim on a share held in [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]] custody, not a share on the company's register ([Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/tokenize); [Base](https://www.base.org/stocks)).
- Offered outside the US only; dividends are reinvested through a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] ([Base](https://www.base.org/stocks)).
- [[concepts/glossary#redeem|Redemption]] terms are set in the issuer documents; check them before relying on redemption ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/overview)).

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

- <https://www.adgm.com/media/announcements/coinbase-establishes-its-tokenization-hub-in-abu-dhabi-with-financial-services-permission-from-the-financial-services-regulatory-authority>

> [!info] At a glance
> **Type:** issuer

> **Chain:** Ethereum, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, (Sei, Solana announced)  
> **Status:** live (US launch 2026-08-04)

*In plain English: Dinari issues tokens backed by US stocks and offers them to eligible US investors.*

On 4 Aug 2026 Dinari launched 724 dShares, including the full S&P 500, to eligible US investors ([Dinari](https://dinari.com/blog/dinari-launches-724-tokenized-stocks-available-to-u-s-investors-and-businesses)). Dinari Inc. is the [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]]; Dinari Securities LLC is the [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]] ([GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/04/3338495/0/en/dinari-inc-opens-platform-licenses-to-u-s-financial-institutions.html)).

US clearing is through Alpaca Securities LLC ([Dinari](https://docs.dinari.com/docs/us)). See [What is a dShare](https://docs.dinari.com/docs/what-is-dshare).

## What this means for holders
- Eligible US investors can buy dShares since 4 Aug 2026 ([Dinari](https://dinari.com/blog/dinari-launches-724-tokenized-stocks-available-to-u-s-investors-and-businesses)).
- Dinari describes its tokens as records that mirror its brokerage books, so your claim runs through Dinari as [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]] ([Dinari SEC input](https://www.sec.gov/files/ctf-written-input-dinari-inc-040226.pdf)).
- Dividends are paid in cash, with [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|USDC]] support ([Dinari](https://dinari.com/blog/dinari-launches-724-tokenized-stocks-available-to-u-s-investors-and-businesses)).

The Figure announcement page blocked retrieval, so only its headline was checked.

## What this means for holders
- Figure's Series A Blockchain Common Stock is SEC-registered stock on the Provenance blockchain, convertible 1:1 into Class A common stock ([424(b)(4)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828026008786/figure-blockchain424b4.htm)).
- It is bought with YLDS, Figure's [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]]-like token, per the [prospectus](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828026008786/figure-blockchain424b4.htm).

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

# Ondo Global Markets (Ondo Stocks)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/ondo-global-markets
description: In plain English: Ondo's stock tokens are notes that track US stocks, backed by shares held at US brokers. They are not the shares themselves.
type: issuer
jurisdiction: British Virgin Islands
chain: Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana
status: unknown
last_updated: 2026-10-29
last_checked: 2026-10-29

> [!info] At a glance
> **Type:** issuer  
> **Jurisdiction:** British Virgin Islands  
> **Chain:** Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana  
> **Status:** unknown  
> **Last updated:** 2026-10-29  

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| name | Ondo Global Markets (Ondo Stocks) |
| jurisdiction | British Virgin Islands |
| product_name | Ondo stock/ETF tokens |
| structure | Structured notes giving economic exposure; no shareholder voting/information rights |
| chains | Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana |
| who_can_buy | Excludes US persons and several jurisdictions; some require qualified/professional status |
| num_assets | 450+ advertised (per Zerion) |

*In plain English: Ondo's stock tokens are notes that track US stocks, backed by shares held at US brokers. They are not the shares themselves.*

Ondo stock tokens are structured notes issued by Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited, backed 1:1 plus a buffer by securities held through US custodial [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealers]] ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory); [trust & transparency](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/trust-and-transparency)).

Eligibility: [Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/eligibility). [[concepts/glossary#redeem|Redemption]]: [Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/investing-and-redeeming). Asset count (450+) is from Zerion (secondary).

The issuer is a [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]] BVI [[concepts/glossary#spv|SPV]]; assets are held at U.S. broker-dealers, overcollateralized, with Ankura as security agent ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)). Tokens are [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]] on [[concepts/glossary#ethereum|Ethereum]] and BNB Chain and [[concepts/glossary#token-2022|Token-2022]] on [[concepts/glossary#solana|Solana]] ([Ondo](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)).

[[concepts/glossary#mint|Mint]] and redeem use signed quotes through IGMTokenManager ([Ondo API](https://docs.ondo.finance/api-reference/overview)).

On 7 Oct 2026 Assetera, an Austrian MiFID II firm, listed 100+ Ondo tokenized stocks and ETFs for eligible investors in 30 EEA countries, widening to 450+ through Q4 2026 ([Assetera](https://www.assetera.com/media/assetera-x-ondo)).

On 27 Oct 2026 Ondo put 15 Ondo Stocks on [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens|Robinhood Chain]] via the Ondo Bridge (minting and redemption stay on Ethereum and BNB Chain). 11 of them, including NVDAon, SPYon, TSLAon and QQQon, sit in Uniswap v4 StablePair pools against the matching Robinhood Stock Token, with dynamic LP fees when the pair drifts from its expected rate. Ondo pitches this as a weekend supply and exit route while Robinhood's mint and redeem window is closed. Ondo also says it has \$1.3B in total value locked and over 450,000 cumulative holders (issuer claims) ([Ondo](https://ondo.finance/blog/ondo-stocks-live-on-robinhood-chain-and-uniswap)).

## What this means for holders
- You hold a structured note from a BVI [[concepts/glossary#spv|SPV]], described as [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]] and overcollateralized by assets held at US [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealers]] ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)).
- Not offered to US persons; buying requires [[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]] ([eligibility](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/eligibility)).
- How minting and [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redemption]] work is set out in [Ondo's docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/investing-and-redeeming).

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

## DTCC ecosystem
Ondo is named among the collaborators and partners in DTCC's Tokenization Service ecosystem at its 28 Oct 2026 launch ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]]; [DTCC](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live)).

| structure | Debt securities |
| chains | Robinhood Chain |
| who_can_buy | Not US, Canada, UK, Switzerland; other restrictions apply |
| num_assets | 190+ (Robinhood) |

*In plain English: Robinhood's stock tokens are debt securities that track a stock's price. They give you no shareholder rights.*

Stock Tokens are tokenised debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited under a [base prospectus](https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/rhj_base_prospectus.pdf); they give economic exposure without rights in the underlying ([docs](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/stock-tokens/); [product page](https://robinhood.com/rhj/stocktokens/)). Separately, EU **Classic** Stock Tokens are MiFID II derivatives ([FAQ](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/)).

On Robinhood Chain, trading at launch is via [[concepts/glossary#rfq|RFQ]] plus [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|AMMs]] and Lighter, with onchain price feeds ([Robinhood](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/)). Mainnet announcement: [Arbitrum](https://blog.arbitrum.io/robinhood-chain-mainnet/).

## Adoption
Bitwise's Q4 2026 staking report says average daily Stock Token volume on Robinhood Chain rose 22x from July to September 2026, and that the chain earned over \$50M in fees in its first quarter ([Bitwise](https://bitwiseinvestments.com/crypto-market-insights/the-bitwise-staking-report-q4-2026), analysis; summary page only, the full report was not retrieved). Monthly volumes of \$526M (July), \$2.21B (August) and \$11.31B (September) come from [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tokenized-stocks-us-companies-object.html) citing Bitwise (news; unverified, not on Bitwise's summary page).

On 14 Sep 2026 Robinhood's CEO said in-kind redemption and voting are coming for Robinhood Stock Tokens; neither was available as of 25 Oct 2026 ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/09/14/robinhood-plans-share-redemptions-voting-rights-for-stock-tokens-after-criticism), news).

Since 27 Oct 2026, 11 Robinhood Stock Tokens (e.g. NVDArh) have Uniswap v4 StablePair pools against the matching [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo]] token on Robinhood Chain. Ondo notes that when Robinhood's mint and redeem window is closed, Stock Tokens keep trading onchain but supply can't expand and holders can't redeem, which can cause price gaps; the pools give an exit through Ondo's 24/7 redemption ([Ondo](https://ondo.finance/blog/ondo-stocks-live-on-robinhood-chain-and-uniswap), issuer blog).

## What this means for holders
- Robinhood Stock Tokens are tokenised debt securities from Robinhood Assets Jersey: you get economic exposure to the stock, with no rights in the underlying share ([Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/rhj/stocktokens/); [docs](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/stock-tokens/)).
- In the EU, Classic Stock Tokens are MiFID II derivative contracts with Robinhood Europe inside Robinhood's app ([Robinhood EU FAQ](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/)).
- Not offered to US persons ([Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/rhj/stocktokens/)).

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

# Securitize (issuer-sponsored shares)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/securitize
description: In plain English: Securitize acts as transfer agent and tokenization platform for funds and companies that issue tokens.
type: issuer
jurisdiction: unknown
chain: Algorand (Exodus), Ethereum (per Zerion, secondary), Solana (per Zerion, secondary), Avalanche (per Zerion, secondary)
status: live (Securitize Stocks launched 2026-10-08)
last_updated: 2026-10-28
last_checked: 2026-10-28

> [!info] At a glance
> **Type:** issuer  
> **Jurisdiction:** unknown  
> **Chain:** Algorand (Exodus), Ethereum (per Zerion, secondary), Solana (per Zerion, secondary), Avalanche (per Zerion, secondary)  
> **Status:** live (Securitize Stocks launched 2026-10-08)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| name | Securitize (issuer-sponsored shares) |

| chains | Algorand (Exodus), Ethereum (per Zerion, secondary), Solana (per Zerion, secondary), Avalanche (per Zerion, secondary) |
| who_can_buy | unknown |
| num_assets | 12 companies at launch (CoinDesk) |

*In plain English: Securitize acts as transfer agent and tokenization platform for funds and companies that issue tokens.*

Example: Exodus Class A common stock tokens on Algorand, with Securitize as [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/exodus-issues-security-token-on-algorand-expanding-access-to-the-growing-digital-security-ecosystem-301304582.html)); trading began on Securitize Markets in March 2022 ([Securitize](https://securitize.io/press-releases/exodus-begins-trading-on-securitize-markets)).

## Securitize Stocks (8 Oct 2026)
Launched stocks as UCC Article 8 security entitlements, 1:1 backed, on [[concepts/glossary#solana|Solana]], settled in USDC, through Securitize's [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]]; Jump makes markets on the PropAMM; conversion to direct registration where available; NYSE and OKXICE venues planned ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html); [RQD](https://rqdclearing.com/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-u-s-stocks-with-security-entitlements/)). The structure is called a convertible [[concepts/glossary#entitlement-token|entitlement token]] (CET). Securitize says it is open to eligible investors in the US, EU and other permitted jurisdictions, the backing shares will not be lent out, and lending and collateral use on markets like Aave is planned ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html)). CoinDesk reported 12 companies at launch ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/10/08/securitize-brings-apple-nvidia-and-tesla-to-solana-with-nyse-trading-in-the-works), news).

## What this means for holders
- Securitize Stocks are UCC Article 8 security entitlements backed 1:1, held through Securitize's broker-dealer, on Solana and settled in USDC ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html)).
- Where available, holders can convert to direct registration, i.e. hold the share on the company's register ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html)).
- Eligible investors in the US, EU and other permitted jurisdictions, subject to local rules ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html)).
- The shares backing the tokens are not lent out ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html)).

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

## DTC direct-registration comment letter (25 Oct 2026)
Securitize's issuer-sponsored tokens (ISTs) record the investor, not [[concepts/glossary#cede-co|Cede & Co.]], as the registered holder on the issuer's books ([Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf)). To turn an existing brokerage position into an IST, the shares must first leave [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] through the [[concepts/glossary#direct-registration-system-drs|Direct Registration System (DRS)]], which today can take several days ([Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf)). Securitize supports DTC's proposal to cut DRS processing "from days to minutes" ([SEC notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20301/self-regulatory-organizations-the-depository-trust-company-notice-of-filing-of-proposed-rule-change)) but asked the SEC for more ([Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf)):
- One instruction that burns a DTC-tokenized position and starts the DRS withdrawal, with a real-time completion message to the transfer agent ("Instant Burn-and-Notify").
- Published DRS processing targets and operating hours, reporting of actual times by stage, and the same modernization for [[concepts/glossary#dwac|DWAC]].
- A timing expectation for brokers to submit customer withdrawal requests, or letting the transfer agent start one on the investor's documented authorization.
- An equally fast path back to [[concepts/glossary#street-name|street name]].
- The tokenization link live by the commercial launch of DTCC's tokenization service, or a published timeline or follow-on filing within three months.

See [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC / DTC tokenization pilot]]. Context: Brett Redfearn's [LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/time-dtc-modernization-now-brett-w-redfearn-a3tse) (28 Oct 2026, opinion).

# xStocks (Backed)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/issuers/xstocks-backed
description: In plain English: xStocks are tokens backed one-for-one by US stocks and ETFs.
type: issuer
jurisdiction: Jersey
chain: Solana, Ethereum, TON, Ink, (Tron, Mantle, BNB Chain announced as coming, Dec 2025)
status: live (since 2025-06-30)
last_updated: 2026-10-25
last_checked: 2026-10-25

> [!info] At a glance
> **Type:** issuer  
> **Jurisdiction:** Jersey  
> **Chain:** Solana, Ethereum, TON, Ink, (Tron, Mantle, BNB Chain announced as coming, Dec 2025)  
> **Status:** live (since 2025-06-30)  
> **Last updated:** 2026-10-25  

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| name | xStocks (Backed) |
| jurisdiction | Jersey |
| product_name | xStocks |
| structure | Tokenized certificates/tracker tokens backed by custodied securities |
| chains | Solana, Ethereum, TON, Ink, (Tron, Mantle, BNB Chain announced as coming, Dec 2025) |
